name: @slatesvideo/mcp-server

tools.name: slates_get_workspace_state
tools.description: Snapshot of the user's Slates workspace: the project list (most recent first) plus the active project in full when you name one. It also returns generationDefaults (the default image and video model and image settings) for when the user states no preference.

limit.description: How many projects to list, newest first. Default 40.

tools.name: slates_get_selection
tools.description: The user's live selection in the Slates app: ticked cards (with codes), the image open in the viewer, and where they are on the open timeline (playhead, selected clips, the clips under the playhead and the words spoken there).

tools.name: slates_set_selection
tools.description: Select cards in Media, Shots on the Board or clips on the timeline, as clicks, Shift-click, Escape and Ctrl/Cmd+A do: replace makes the ids the whole selection, add and remove change only them, clear empties it, all ticks everything the tab shows (Media: the grid as filtered, folded rounds left out; Board: every Shot on the open board; timeline: every clip on the open timeline). Every surface needs a project open in the window, Media its grid showing and the Board the Board or Script tab; slates_set_view opens and switches. On the timeline, clip ids open the Cut on their timeline, scroll to them and open the Inspector on the last, so use it to show the user a clip instead of asking them to click it; all, or replace with no ids, needs a timeline open (slates_set_view cut.timelineId). Ids are asset ids or badge codes (Media), Shot ids or SHOT-A codes (Board) or clip ids from slates_get_timeline (timeline, all on one timeline). Answers with the selection as it settled and names any id it could not select. slates_get_selection reads it back (timeline clips under timeline.selectedClips); what is selected is what the user means by 'these'.

ids.description: Asset ids or codes (media), Shot ids or codes (board) or clip ids (timeline). Not used by clear or all.

tools.name: slates_get_view
tools.description: What the user is looking at in Slates: Home or a project, the tab (Media, Script or Board), the open board and its View and Filter, Media's tab, chosen folder and narrowing, a Library page, the picture viewer, the timeline Viewer's mode and clip, Compare, the animatic, Settings, whether the prompt box is hidden, the timeline and the side panels, and, from a desktop with the one-window layout, the window's layout (Plan or Edit, which areas show, the Viewer's Inspector drawer open or shut for want of room), and any dialog or menu open over the page. New desktops also report cut.format and the selected variant grid rows and aspects. Read it before telling the user where to click.

tools.name: slates_set_view
tools.description: Change what the user is looking at, as their own clicks would: open a project or go Home, switch tab, open a board, jump to a scene, set the Board's View and Filter, set Media's tab, folder and narrowing, jump to a card in Media, open a Library page, a picture in the picture viewer or a clip in the timeline's Viewer, Compare, the animatic or Settings on a pane, show or hide the prompt box, open or park the timeline or switch the cut on it, open a Shot's panel on Script, set the side panels (the project navigator and its folded sections, the Slates Director panel), the Script page's Words or Words + shots and its text size, the Board's card size and linked clips, and on a desktop with the one-window layout the layout and which areas show. Only the fields you name change; the app clamps sizes, answers with what it settled on, and names any field it could not apply. A project change is applied alone (it restores that project's own view). Use it when the user asks you to show or open something, not to answer a question they can see for themselves.

projectId.description: Open this project, or null for Home. Applied alone.

full.description: Give the timeline the whole workspace.

side.description: Where the timeline is parked; picking a side opens the timeline. On a desktop with the one-window layout it always runs along the bottom: another side comes back as a note and is not applied.

height.description: The bottom band's height in px.

width.description: The side column's width in px; with the one-window layout, the Viewer's width in the Plan layout.

timelineId.description: The named cut to show on the timeline (slates_list_timelines).

format.description: Preview this delivery format; requires ad-variant-export.

items.description: Delivery format id from slates_get_variant_grid.formats; the desktop validates it and supplies dimensions.

gridSelection.description: Selected existing grid rows and delivery formats; requires ad-variant-export. Does not export.

folded.description: Every section to fold to its title (storyboards is Boards); a section not named unfolds. Applies to the open project.

leftDock.description: The project navigator on the left.

studioAgent.description: The Slates Director panel on the right. It cannot be opened while the agent is off in Settings.

details.description: Words + shots (true): each shot's picture beside its words on the Script page. Words (false): the words alone.

textScale.description: The page's text size; 1 is the default.

panelShotId.description: Open this Shot's details panel on the Script page (it binds the Shot to the prompt box, as a click does); null closes it.

id.description: Open this board (on Board and Script).

sceneId.description: Scroll the Board to this scene.

level.description: View: Film (posters), Scenes (the working card) or Shot (each card open).

cardWidth.description: Card width in px, anywhere between the stops.

filter.description: Filter: every shot, only shots with a linked clip, or only shots without one.

linkedClips.description: Show the row of linked clips under each shot.

scriptFollowsDrag.description: The board menu's Script follows a drag.

collapsedSceneIds.description: Every scene to fold; a scene not named unfolds.

folderId.description: Choose this folder (new pictures land in it), or null for all media.

unfiledOnly.description: Show only media in no folder.

linkedOnly.description: Images tab: only pictures with a linked video.

revealAssetId.description: Jump to this card in Media, undoing only what hides it (the app says what it changed).

library.description: Open a Library category's page in Media's place; null goes back to the grid.

assetId.description: A picture opens in the picture viewer; a clip plays in the timeline's Viewer (Source), on desktops after 1.6.2. null closes the picture viewer.

mode.description: What the timeline's Viewer shows: source (a clip opened to watch) or timeline (the timeline). Compare opens through compare.open. Desktops from 1.6.3.

assetIds.description: The compare set, two to four items.

animatic.description: Play the board as a rough cut from a Shot (the Board or Script tab must be showing).

settings.description: Open Settings, on a pane (ai is AI tools, keys is API keys).

composer.description: Show or hide the prompt box.

layout.description: edit gives the Viewer the room, with Media, Board and Script a column at its left; plan gives it to them, with the Viewer a column at their right.

inspector.description: Open or shut the Inspector, the Viewer's drawer (opening it shows the Viewer); in a window with no room, Media, Board and Script fold to make room.

lensWidth.description: The Media, Board and Script column's width in px in the Edit layout.

window.description: The one window (desktops with it): its layout and which areas show.

tools.name: slates_get_manual_picture
tools.description: A picture of a Slates screen from the app manual, with numbered callouts and their legend, taken from the version the user runs. Pass the picture id the manual names (app-manual sections show "Picture `id`"); no id lists them. Show one when the user cannot find something or asks what a screen looks like; never unasked. When the control is on screen, slates_highlight_control points at the real thing instead.

id.description: Picture id from the manual, e.g. "window-overview". Omit to list.

tools.name: slates_highlight_control
tools.description: Point at a control in the user's Slates window: a grey outline around it for a few seconds, with your caption beside it. It clicks nothing and never changes the view; the user's next click clears it. Target ids are listed at the end of each app-manual surface section ("controls you can point at"), or pass list:true to get every id with whether it is on screen now. shown:false means it is not on screen: tell the user the way there, or open that view with slates_set_view if they want you to.

caption.description: A few words shown beside it, e.g. "Click here to open the timeline".

list.description: Return every target id, its on-screen name, where it is, and whether it is on screen now.

tools.name: slates_get_composer
tools.description: What the prompt box holds right now, as the user sees it: the lane and model, whether it is editing a Shot or a draft, the words, every setting with the values it offers, each reference tile with its number, role and whether the model's limit leaves it out, the exact text the model receives (See what gets sent), mentions that match nothing, the notice line, and the Generate button's price. Read it before telling the user what a press will do, or before staging with slates_set_composer.

tools.name: slates_set_composer
tools.description: Stage a request in the user's prompt box, as their own clicks would, and leave it for them to press Generate: edit a Shot in it or stop, clear or restore the draft, reuse a result's prompt, edit a clip, pick the lane and model, write the words, attach pictures, clips or audio with roles, re-file or remove them, set settings and the voice, fill Lip Sync or Motion Control's inputs. It never generates and never spends; the answer is the box as it settled (the same report as slates_get_composer) plus a line for anything it could not apply and why. Use it when the user wants a setup ready to look at; to generate yourself, quote with slates_estimate_generation_cost and use the generate ops.

projectId.description: The project you expect the box to be in; refused if another is open.

bindShotId.description: Edit this Shot in the box (id or code; every change is saved to it); null stops editing and brings the draft back.

clear.description: Empty the unsaved draft; restoreDraft undoes it. Not while a Shot is bound.

restoreDraft.description: Put back the draft that Clear, Reuse prompt or Edit with AI replaced (they swap).

restoreSetup.description: On a bound Shot, swap back the setup Continue replaced (writes the Shot; again swaps back).

fromAssetId.description: Reuse prompt: this result's recipe replaces the box (id or code).

editSourceAssetId.description: Edit with AI: this clip becomes the canvas and the box starts clean.

lane.description: The Image / Video / Audio tab; it lands on the last model used there.

model.description: A model id (slates_list_available_models), `<id>::face` for its Face row, `chatgpt`, `lip-sync` or `motion-transfer`.

prompt.description: Replaces the words. @name and #name attach what they name, as typing does.

addMentions.description: @name / #name added at the end of the words (slates_list_library gives each item its mention).

attach.description: Pictures, clips or audio from the project (id or code). A picture with no role goes in as a dropped one does; a clip is a video-reference, audio an audio-reference.

detach.description: Take these out of the box: asset ids or codes, or a character's id to drop the voice her @mention brought.

setRole.description: Re-file pictures already in the box, as a tile's role menu does.

params.description: Settings by id, each to a value it offers (slates_get_composer lists both), applied after the model.

voice.description: The voice on a voice model: a preset (slates_list_voices), an audio clip in the project, or described in words.

sourceAssetId.description: Lip Sync: the picture or clip with the face; null clears it.

speechText.description: Lip Sync, Text to speech: the words spoken (Speech Text).

drivingVideoAssetId.description: Motion Control: the clip whose motion is copied (Motion).

characterImageAssetId.description: Motion Control: the picture to animate (Character).

tool.description: Lip Sync and Motion Control inputs (pick model lip-sync or motion-transfer first). An uploaded audio file is only the user.

tools.name: slates_reorder_folders
tools.description: Reorder the Folders section of the left dock, as dragging a row does. Pass folder ids in the new order; ones you leave out keep their order after them.

tools.name: slates_reorder_pins
tools.description: Reorder the Pinned section of the left dock, as dragging a pin does. Pass the pinned images (UUIDs or badge codes) in the new order; ones you leave out keep their order after them.

tools.name: slates_get_usage
tools.description: What Settings → Account → Usage shows: estimated spend across every project for this month (default), the last 7 days or all time, the image and video counts, video seconds and the models spent on most.

tools.name: slates_get_app_settings
tools.description: The app's own settings an agent may read: the app version, the projects folder, which tab a never-opened project lands on (newProjectLens), whether ChatGPT images is on, and (from Slates 1.6.1) who does Slates Director's thinking (studioAgentHost: slates, codex or claude) with each host's model and thinking level ('' is its default). Never keys or sign-in.

tools.name: slates_set_app_settings
tools.description: Change an app setting the user asked you to: newProjectLens (the tab a never-opened project lands on: media, script or board), chatGptImagesEnabled (Settings → AI tools → ChatGPT images), or who does Slates Director's thinking: studioAgentHost (slates, codex for the user's own Codex on their ChatGPT plan, claude for their own Claude Code on their Claude plan) and each host's model and thinking level, ids from the host's own list or '' for its default. The projects folder, keys and sign-in are the user's to change.

tools.name: slates_get_spend_limits
tools.description: The project's spend limit and this session's budget, in credits, where a session is this MCP connection or CLI run and a new one starts at the full default budget: each limit (null is none), what is spent against it and what is left, as shown beside Generate. A generation over either one is refused with its cost and what is left; read this before a run of generations.

tools.name: slates_set_spend_limits
tools.description: Set the project's spend limit or this session's budget (per MCP connection or CLI run, not across them), in credits; null removes one. Lowering a limit is yours to do. Raising or removing one, the session budget included, needs the user's OK in chat first: without confirm it changes nothing and returns requires_confirm. Pass confirm=true only after the user says yes, never on your own.

projectLimitCredits.description: What this project may spend in all, by hand and by every agent.

sessionBudgetCredits.description: What this MCP connection or CLI run may spend.

confirm.description: Set true only to relay the user's explicit OK to raise or remove a limit.

tools.name: slates_get_asset
tools.description: One asset in full (UUID or badge code): its recorded prompt, model, settings and inputs, its source picture and linked clips, and how many clips and board shots use it. slates_list_assets rows are compact; read this before reusing or explaining one card.

tools.name: slates_link_asset_source
tools.description: Link a clip to the picture it came from, as the clip card's Link video to image does (it adds a link; a clip can have several), or pass imageAssetId null to unlink it from every picture. UUIDs or badge codes.

assetId.description: The clip.

imageAssetId.description: The picture, or null to unlink.

tools.name: slates_transcribe_asset
tools.description: Transcribe a video or audio asset's speech into words timed to within a frame, as the card's Transcribe command does. Free: it runs on the user's machine and spends no credits. The first run downloads the speech models once (the result's downloadedModelsMB says how much) and can take minutes; if the call times out, the desktop keeps working, so read slates_get_asset_transcript before trying again. A repeat, or another asset with the same bytes, reuses the stored transcript (reused: true); force re-runs it, and an edited transcript (edited: true) is kept unless forced. noSpeech: true means the audio holds no speech. slates_add_captions transcribes on its own, so call this when you want the words themselves.

assetId.description: A video or audio asset: its code (VID-V3) or id.

force.description: Transcribe again even when a stored transcript exists.

tools.name: slates_get_asset_transcript
tools.description: Read an asset's stored transcript: its words with their times in the asset's own seconds, whether it holds speech, whether the user edited it, and when it was made. Never transcribes: transcript null with a hint means nobody has transcribed it yet (slates_transcribe_asset, free).

assetId.description: A video or audio asset: its code (VID-V3) or id.

tools.name: slates_edit_asset_transcript
tools.description: Correct an asset's transcript by sending its whole text back, edited, as the transcript editor in the app does: a corrected word keeps its time, a removed word goes, and a new word takes time shared out from its neighbours (the silence between them, or the word before it). Paragraph breaks are free; only the words count. By default the captions heard from this asset are made again from the corrected words, on the same tracks in the same style (recaption false skips that); captions estimated from the Shot's line or written from your own words are left alone. Read the current text first with slates_get_asset_transcript. Free. The machine's own words stay stored, so slates_transcribe_asset with force starts fresh.

assetId.description: A video or audio asset with a transcript: its code (VID-V3) or id.

text.description: The whole transcript, edited. Words are separated by spaces or line breaks.

recaption.description: Make this asset's captions again from the edited words. Default true.

tools.name: slates_cut_by_transcript
tools.description: Cut words or pauses out of a video or audio clip on the timeline by its transcript, as Cut on the clip's Transcript page does: each stretch leaves the clip, which splits around it, and the gap closes (ripple), at the clip's own in point and speed. Name words by their index in slates_get_asset_transcript's words (from and to, inclusive), pauses by the index of the word each follows, or stretches of the file's own seconds. A word's cut reaches up to 60 ms before it and 100 ms after it into silence, never into a neighbouring word; a pause keeps 100 ms after the word before and 60 ms before the word after, so no word loses its first or last sound. The clip's linked sound and the captions heard from it are cut the same way; trackIds adds more lanes (a picture above it, a music bed) to keep in sync; linked false cuts only the clip's lane. Words an earlier cut left in later pieces are found there. Returns the clips written, ids deleted, durationFrames, each stretch cut in timeline seconds (latest first), removedSec, and timing: aligned words land within a frame or two, recognizer words within about a quarter second (transcribe again with force first). Free. Requires transcript-cut; update Slates on capability refusal.

clipId.description: The video or audio clip on the timeline whose words to cut.

words.description: Runs of words to cut, by index in the asset's transcript words, from and to inclusive.

pauses.description: Pauses to cut, each by the index of the word it follows.

ranges.description: Stretches of the file's own seconds to cut, as the transcript counts them.

linked.description: False: cut only the clip's lane, not its linked sound's. Default true.

trackIds.description: More lanes to cut and close up the same way, to keep them in sync.

tools.name: slates_get_beat_grid
tools.description: Read a music file's beat grid, to check it before cutting to it: every beat in the file's own seconds with its downbeat flag and a confidence from 0 to 1 (hand-placed beats read 1), a summary (BPM, beats a bar, the tempo sections, whether the tempo changes), lowConfidence (the spans to check: runs of unsure beats, and gaps where the tempo says a beat belongs) and the hand edits kept on it. With a clipId it also gives onTimeline: where each beat lands on the cut, in frames, at the clip's in point and speed. picture true saves a PNG of the grid over the waveform (downbeats bright with bar numbers, unsure beats amber) and returns its path; fromSec and toSec frame a stretch. Look at it to judge a span. Never finds beats: beats null with a hint means none yet (slates_find_beats, free). Fix a wrong beat with slates_edit_beat_grid. Requires beat-grid; update Slates on capability refusal.

assetId.description: An audio or video asset: its code (AUD-A2) or id. Or name clipId.

clipId.description: A clip on the timeline: the grid of its file, plus where each beat lands on the cut (onTimeline, in frames).

picture.description: Save a picture of the grid over the waveform and return its path.

fromSec.description: The picture's first second, in the file's own time.

toSec.description: The picture's last second, in the file's own time.

tools.name: slates_find_beats
tools.description: Find a music file's beats, downbeats and tempo on the user's machine, as Find beats in the clip's Inspector does. Free: it spends no credits and nothing leaves the machine. The first run downloads the beat model once (the result's downloadedModelMB says how much) and can take a few minutes; if the call times out, the desktop keeps working, so read slates_get_beat_grid before trying again. Hand edits already on the grid are kept and applied over the new beats. Returns the grid as slates_get_beat_grid does; read its lowConfidence spans before you cut. Requires beat-grid; update Slates on capability refusal.

assetId.description: An audio or video asset: its code (AUD-A2) or id. Or name clipId.

clipId.description: A clip on the timeline: the grid of its file, plus where each beat lands on the cut (onTimeline, in frames).

tools.name: slates_edit_beat_grid
tools.description: Correct a music file's beat grid by hand, as the Beat grid controls in the clip's Inspector do: shift the whole grid (sec), set the downbeat (the beat at a second starts a bar; beatsPerBar sets the meter), lay a tempo over a span (fromSec, toSec, bpm; it works with no grid yet, so a known tempo needs no detection), or add, move or delete one beat. Times are the file's own seconds, as slates_get_beat_grid gives them; a beat is named by the nearest one within 0.15 s. Edits apply in order and are kept: finding the beats again never overwrites them. undo takes back the last edit; clearEdits drops them all. The marks on the clip and the snapping follow at once. Free. Returns the grid as slates_get_beat_grid does. Requires beat-grid; update Slates on capability refusal.

assetId.description: An audio or video asset: its code (AUD-A2) or id. Or name clipId.

clipId.description: A clip on the timeline: the grid of its file, plus where each beat lands on the cut (onTimeline, in frames).

sec.description: Seconds to move every beat; negative is earlier.

at.description: The beat nearest this second starts a bar; the bars around it follow.

beatsPerBar.description: Also set the meter, in beats a bar.

bpm.description: Lay beats at this tempo over the span, from the beat nearest fromSec (or fromSec itself).

from.description: The beat nearest this second moves...

at.description: The beat nearest this second goes.

undo.description: Take back the last hand edit.

clearEdits.description: Drop every hand edit and show the found beats.

tools.name: slates_cut_to_beats
tools.description: Cut a lane to the music, so its cuts land on the beats of a music clip's grid. mode snap (default) rolls each existing cut on the lane (two clips that meet) to the nearest chosen beat within reachFrames (default half a beat), so the edit keeps its order and its length; mode split cuts the lane's clips at every chosen beat. on downbeat uses only the first beat of each bar; every 2 takes every second one; fromFrame and toFrame hold it to a stretch of the timeline. trackId names the lane (default: the first unlocked video lane with clips). Read the grid first (slates_get_beat_grid) and fix any lowConfidence span it lists, or cuts land on wrong beats. Returns the clips written, cuts (clipId, fromFrame, toFrame), skipped (each cut left where it was, and why) and beatFrames. Free. Requires beat-grid; update Slates on capability refusal.

musicClipId.description: The music clip on the timeline whose beats the cuts land on.

trackId.description: The lane to cut. Default: the first unlocked video lane with clips.

mode.description: snap: move the existing cuts onto beats (default). split: cut the clips at every chosen beat.

every.description: Use every Nth chosen beat. Default 1.

fromFrame.description: Only beats from this timeline frame on.

toFrame.description: Only beats up to this timeline frame.

reachFrames.description: snap: how far a cut may move to reach a beat, in frames. Default half a beat.

tools.name: slates_extract_video_frame
tools.description: Save one frame of a clip as a new picture in Media, as the clip card's camera does: at 'first', 'last' (default 'first') or a second. Free. The usual continuity move: extract a clip's last frame and use it as the next clip's first frame. To only look at a clip, use slates_get_asset_video_frames; this one adds a picture to the project.

assetId.description: The clip, UUID or badge code.

tools.name: slates_get_me
tools.description: Identity, license tier, and credit balance for the connected Slates account.

tools.name: slates_get_credit_balance
tools.description: Current credit balance only (credits never expire); slates_get_me also returns identity and license tier. Read it to answer a balance question or to check there is enough for a quoted total.

tools.name: slates_list_available_models
tools.description: Registry of generation model cost keys with per-call credit cost, as a compact "key credits" table. Optional `filter` substring (e.g. "kling" or "nano-banana") keeps the result small — prefer it. For a single known model, slates_estimate_generation_cost is cheaper still.

filter.description: Substring match on the model key, e.g. "kling-v3" or "seedance"

tools.name: slates_estimate_generation_cost
tools.description: Quote credits before any generate_* op. For saved Shots, a board or a scene, quote with slates_get_board_quote instead. Accepts the generation model ids and parameters (edit seats other than Kling, lip-sync and motion-transfer engines need an exact registry cost key), or an exact registry cost key. Show the user the total and wait for their OK before the generate call; the result flags requires_confirm above the threshold and carries the model's prompting card.

model.description: Base model id as passed to the generate op (e.g. "seedance-2", "kling-v3.0-std", "nano-banana-2-1") or an exact registry cost key ("nano-banana-2-1-2k", "seedance-2-1080p-8s")

duration.description: Seconds; cost scales linearly. Required with a video or PER-SECOND audio base id. Per-model windows: see slates_generate_video's duration. Audio: seed-audio 3-120 (⚠️ the requested duration IS the bill), eleven-sfx 1-22. ⛔ NOT for inworld-tts-2 — pass `characters`.

characters.description: inworld-tts-2 only — the LENGTH OF THE TEXT to speak (250-char buckets).

videoResolution.description: Video only. Omitted, each model quotes at its own default. Per-model ladders: see slates_generate_video's videoResolution.

resolution.description: Image only. Omit for the model default; pass the same value to generation.

aspectRatio.description: GPT Image: the frame shape changes the price; pass the generation's value.

sound.description: Kling 3.0: a silent take prices differently from one with sound. Omitted means sound on, as generation bills it; pass false to price a silent take. Kling 4K keys include audio.

seedanceFace.description: Seedance Face row, for an AI character's face.

seedanceRealFace.description: Seedance with a consented real person (premium key).

videoRefSeconds.description: Combined reference-video seconds, measured from the clips.

audioRefSeconds.description: Combined reference-audio seconds, including attached character voices.

referenceImages.description: MiniMax H3 rows only — how many reference IMAGES the generation will carry. Each image past the row's free allowance is a paid dimension of the cost key, so a quote that omits this UNDER-REPORTS a reference-heavy job. The allowances differ: minimax-h3 gives 5 free, minimax-h3-max gives 4. Ignored by every other model. Start/end frames are free on both rows and are not reference images.

tools.name: slates_list_projects
tools.description: Full records for every project in the desktop workspace, unbounded. To start a session use slates_get_workspace_state instead: the compact list, the active project and generation defaults.

tools.name: slates_create_project
tools.description: Create a new Slates project, only when the user asks for one; otherwise work in the current project (slates_get_workspace_state). Returns the new project record.

tools.name: slates_get_project
tools.description: Get a Slates project by id.

tools.name: slates_list_assets
tools.description: List assets in a Slates project as compact rows (id, code, label, type) — newest first, default limit 50. Each asset carries its short code (IMG-A12 / VID-V3 / AUD-S1 — the badge the user sees on the gallery card) and label. When the user names an asset by code ("use IMG-A36 as the reference"), pass it as `search` to resolve the assetId. Always speak about assets by code + label, never by UUID. A favorited asset carries `isFavorite: true` (absent means not favorited). Generate results already return new asset ids, so do not list to find one you just created.

search.description: Case-insensitive match on code or label (e.g. "IMG-A36" or "sunset")

tools.name: slates_get_asset_image
tools.description: Read an asset image off disk and return it inline as base64 so the calling LLM sees the actual pixels. The response also carries the asset's short code (e.g. IMG-A12) and human label; use these when referring to the asset in chat with the user (e.g. "I'm using IMG-A12 — Beach Sunset as the first frame") so they can match it to the badged thumbnail in the Slates gallery. Default JPEG 85% ≤1024px long-edge for token economy. Pass fullRes=true for the original PNG. Takes the asset UUID, not a badge code.

tools.name: slates_get_assets_batch
tools.description: Fetch up to 8 image-asset thumbnails inline in a single call. Use this when picking the right reference from a project gallery — one round trip beats N. Each returned image carries its short code (IMG-A12) and label. Video assets are not supported here — call slates_get_asset_video_frames for those.

ids.description: 1-8 image-asset UUIDs (not badge codes). Order is preserved in the response.

tools.name: slates_get_asset_video_frames
tools.description: Extract evenly-spaced sampled still frames from a video asset and return them inline as JPEGs. Inspect visible appearance, composition and identity before revising a prompt. Stills do not verify continuous motion, timing, lip sync or sound; actual playback through a capable host is needed for those claims. Default 3 samples; count can request more. The response includes the asset code and label; use them when discussing the clip.

id.description: Asset UUID, not a badge code: pass the code to slates_list_assets as search to resolve it.

count.description: Number of frames to extract. Default 3.

tools.name: slates_upload_reference_image
tools.description: Add a reference image, video clip, or audio file to a Slates project from disk. Pass either filePath (absolute path to a local file) or dataUrl (base64 data: URL) — exactly one. Set type:"video" to bring in a clip (the user's own footage to edit/relocate/trim) or type:"audio" for music/VO/SFX they already have; both are probed on ingest, so duration (and for video, dimensions) are available immediately, and audio gets its waveform. A camera clip the timeline cannot play smoothly (ProRes, HEVC, 4K, sparse keyframes) answers playableCopy {state:"making", percent}: the timeline plays that copy once it is made, while export and generation read the original, so nothing waits on it. Default type is "image". dataUrl is image-only. Pass label to name it and note to record what it is; without them it is "Imported file". A picture derived from a project asset (edited, masked, upscaled or converted outside Slates) belongs in slates_save_external_image with referenceAssetIds, so its source and prompt are recorded.

type.description: Asset kind for a filePath import — "image" (default), "video", or "audio". A dataUrl is always an image.

folderId.description: Folder the result lands in (slates_list_folders). Omit it to follow the folder chosen in the user's Slates window, else the project root; null is the root, on purpose.

label.description: The name shown on the asset card and in lists, with its code, e.g. "Ref: copper No".

note.description: What the asset is, stored as the asset's prompt text and read back by slates_get_asset.

tools.name: slates_update_asset
tools.description: Rename an asset (its label, shown with its code on its card and in lists) and/or replace the note stored as its prompt text. UUID or badge code. A note changes only an upload or a picture saved from an external host; a generated asset keeps the prompt that made it but can still be renamed.

label.description: The name shown on the asset card and in lists, with its code, e.g. "Ref: copper No".

note.description: What the asset is, stored as the asset's prompt text and read back by slates_get_asset.

tools.name: slates_save_external_image
tools.description: Save an image generated by an external host with its exact prompt, generator, reference images and measured dimensions. This does not generate or spend Slates credits. Pass filePath or dataUrl for a new result, or assetId to annotate an existing upload in place. Ordinary pasted or dragged files belong to slates_upload_reference_image. Only name a model if the host reported it; requestedSettings records requests, not verified output settings.

tools.name: slates_get_chatgpt_status
tools.description: Check whether the local Codex host is installed, signed in with ChatGPT, and supports built-in image generation. Does not generate or charge Slates credits.

tools.name: slates_connect_chatgpt
tools.description: Start Codex-managed ChatGPT sign-in and return a browser sign-in URL for the user. Call only when the user requests connecting their account. Never ask for credentials or tokens.

tools.name: slates_generate_chatgpt_image
tools.description: Generate an image through the local Codex host using the connected ChatGPT account, then save it in Slates with its exact submitted prompt, reference lineage and measured dimensions. Uses ChatGPT account limits, never Slates credits or a paid API fallback. Check slates_get_chatgpt_status first. Supply a new UUID requestId once per intended generation; reuse it for retries to avoid duplicate generation/import. No explicit image model, quality or size controls are exposed. Prompt may request visual properties without guaranteeing them. Background returns a generationId for slates_get_generation_status. After an error, start no new run unless the user asks; a retry reuses the same requestId.

aspectRatio.description: Optional framing request appended verbally to the prompt, not an exact output-size guarantee.

folderId.description: Folder the result lands in (slates_list_folders). Omit it to follow the folder chosen in the user's Slates window, else the project root; null is the root, on purpose.

tools.description: List asset folders in a project.

tools.name: slates_move_assets_to_folder

tools.name: slates_set_asset_favorite
tools.description: Mark or unmark one asset as a favorite. The heart persists on the card in the app, and slates_list_assets reports it as isFavorite.

assetId.description: Asset UUID, not a badge code: pass the code to slates_list_assets as search to resolve it.

tools.name: slates_export_assets
tools.description: Copy the ORIGINAL files of one or more assets (images, clips or audio) into a directory on this machine, named by their codes (IMG-A12.png). Never overwrites: a clash gets -2, -3. The project is untouched. Works for an image-only project with no shot, video or timeline. Returns each exported path and any asset whose file is missing.

assetIds.description: Asset UUID, not a badge code: pass the code to slates_list_assets as search to resolve it.

directory.description: Absolute path; created if it does not exist.

tools.name: slates_list_pins
tools.description: List a project's pinned references: the images kept in the dock's Pinned section, one click from the prompt. A pin attaches nothing to a generation by itself.

tools.name: slates_pin_references
tools.description: Pin one or more images to the dock's Pinned section (UUIDs or badge codes like IMG-A8). Already-pinned ones are reported, not doubled. Pinning keeps a picture at hand; pass it as a reference to a generation to actually use it.

assetIds.description: Image assets, UUIDs or badge codes.

tools.name: slates_unpin_reference
tools.description: Take one image off the dock's Pinned section. The image stays in the project.

assetId.description: UUID or badge code.

tools.name: slates_move_assets_to_project
tools.description: Move assets (images, videos, audio) out of one project into another. The media files move on disk into the destination project folder — this is a real re-home, not a copy. Moved assets leave whatever gallery folder they were in and are issued fresh badge codes in the destination.

tools.name: slates_copy_assets_to_project
tools.description: Copy assets (images, videos, audio) from one project into another. The originals stay exactly where they are — new files, new rows, new badge codes in the destination. Use this instead of slates_move_assets_to_project when the asset is already in use where it lives: an image that is a character, location or look picture, or sits in a board frame, CANNOT be moved out (that would leave the other project pointing at a file it no longer owns), but it can always be copied. Lineage is not copied; the copy starts clean.

tools.name: slates_move_entity_to_project
tools.description: Move a Library item (a character, location, product, look…) into another project, taking every image it references with it; it lands in the target's category of the same name. This is the fix when slates_move_assets_to_project refuses an asset because a Library item still uses it: the image can't leave on its own, but the whole item can. Refuses (rather than cascading) if one of its images is also used by something else; then use slates_copy_library_item_to_project to copy the whole item, or slates_copy_assets_to_project for the images alone. mentioningShots lists this project's Shots that mention it: they keep the words and fire without it until it comes back. Board frames are not movable this way; moving a frame's image out would empty the shot.

kind.description: Optional and ignored: every value means a Library item. Kept for older callers.

tools.name: slates_list_characters

tools.name: slates_set_character_identity_asset

assetId.description: Asset UUID, not a badge code: pass the code to slates_list_assets as search to resolve it.

tools.name: slates_list_environments
tools.description: List the locations (environments) in a Slates project. These are Library items: slates_list_library lists them with every other Library item, each with its category and mention (@name; looks #name).

tools.description: Create a new location (environment) in a Slates project. These are Library items: slates_create_library_item creates one in a category you choose and returns its @mention.

style.description: Art style. Omitted: keeps the reference's medium (Slates 1.6.2 and older use realistic). Canonical styles: photoreal, anime, painterly, 3d-render, comic. Or pass any free-text instruction, e.g. 'turn this into a real person'.

tools.name: slates_generate_character_identity
tools.description: Generate one identity sheet (a portrait plus front and back full-body views) from a base portrait and bind it as the item's canonical picture. Works on a character or any Library thing; the item must exist (slates_create_character or slates_create_library_item). Craft: slates-character-identity. Show the user the estimate from slates_estimate_generation_cost and wait for their OK before calling: this tool has no confirm gate.

characterId.description: A character, or the id of any Library thing: both sheet tools run on any thing, and the result binds as its image.

baseAssetId.description: The base portrait asset the identity is generated from. Asset UUID, not a badge code: pass the code to slates_list_assets as search to resolve it.

userNotes.description: Extra instruction, e.g. "use the woman on the left".

model.description: Image model for the sheet. Omit for the sheet tool's seat (gpt-image-2-5-sunburst), which is what the app's own button uses. Pass another only to compare seats side by side.

tools.name: slates_generate_environment_plate
tools.description: Generate one clean, empty establishing image of a place from an optional base image and bind it as the item's canonical picture. Works on a location or any Library thing; the item must exist (slates_create_environment or slates_create_library_item). Show the user the estimate from slates_estimate_generation_cost and wait for their OK before calling: this tool has no confirm gate.

environmentId.description: A location, or the id of any Library thing: both sheet tools run on any thing, and the result binds as its image.

baseAssetId.description: Optional base image to establish from (e.g. a rough location shot).

tools.name: slates_list_storyboards
tools.description: List the boards (storyboards) in a Slates project.

tools.name: slates_create_storyboard
tools.description: Create a new board (storyboard) with a default first scene. Returns the board record.

tools.name: slates_get_storyboard_with_frames
tools.description: Deep-fetch a board: every scene, every slot, and the SHOT in each slot — its script line, references, model, params and takes — plus the piece's variety distribution. This is the same board, in the same order, that the user is reading.

tools.name: slates_add_scene
tools.description: Add a new scene to a board.

tools.name: slates_add_frame
tools.description: Park an EXISTING image in a scene as a new slot. It creates a Shot for that picture automatically, because a scene is a list of Shots. To write a beat — line, references, model, prompt — use slates_create_shot instead; it needs no image and files itself.

assetId.description: Asset UUID, not a badge code: pass the code to slates_list_assets as search to resolve it.

tools.name: slates_generate_image
tools.description: Generate an image via Slates credits. Pass projectId to save into a Slates project (asset appears live in the desktop UI). All models except nano-banana-2-1 require projectId (no headless path). Pass aspectRatio (the server returns requires_clarification when missing); resolution defaults to the model's own. Show the user the estimate and wait for their OK before any generation, however small. Cost above 17 credits, or any referenceAssetIds, also returns requires_confirm — pass confirm=true only to relay that OK. MCP/CLI generation always charges credits. The estimate returns the model's prompting card; load its slates-prompting-* guide with slates_get_prompting_guide for anything the card leaves out.

model.description:
Image model. Omitted: gpt-image-2-5-sunburst with projectId, nano-banana-2-1 (the only headless seat) without.
Nano Banana 2.1: The all-rounder and the only image seat with a headless path: holds many subjects coherently in one frame, keeps what an edit leaves alone, and is the start-frame for legible in-scene text. It reasons before it draws, so dense compositions and hero frames land without a premium tier.
GPT Image 2.5 Flare: THE FAST GPT IMAGE SEAT — OpenAI's small model, optimized for SPEED, quality COMPARABLE to GPT Image 2 (not better) at roughly half the latency. Route here when speed matters: drafts, exploration, volume. TEXT / DIAGRAM / PANEL work — character sheets, shot grids, text-bearing panels. When quality outranks speed, escalate to Sunburst. Own content filter, distinct from Gemini's. Killed by a head-to-head at the intended crop going the other way.
GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst: THE QUALITY GPT IMAGE SEAT — OpenAI's most capable image model, higher quality than GPT Image 2, same price as Flare, deliberately SLOWER. Route here unless speed is the point: finals, hero frames, photoreal people, and multi-reference edits where every reference must survive into one frame — its widest lead. Explore on Flare, finish on Sunburst.
FLUX 3 Image: The premium less-filtered image seat: photoreal frames, precise layout and in-image text, at its loosest safety setting, which can still reject a prompt. Auto-routes to its edit endpoint when references are present.
Seedream 5 Lite: Cheapest flat-priced image seat (GPT Image 2.5 at low quality costs less per image). Less filtered, though it can still reject a prompt. Routes to its edit endpoint when references are present.
Full table: the slates-model-selection skill.

projectId.description: Save into this Slates project. Renderer refreshes live. Required for every model except nano-banana-2-1.

resolution.description: Omit for the selected model default. Override for a specific delivery size; use the same setting when estimating.

quality.description: GPT Image only. Default high; estimate the chosen tier before generation.

backgroundMode.description: GPT Image only. transparent = alpha channel. Free.

aspectRatio.description: Pick from the use case: cinematic 16:9 · TikTok/Reels 9:16 · IG square 1:1 · ultra-wide 21:9. 1:1 costs most on GPT Image. Per model: nano-banana-2-1/flux-3/seedream-5-lite: 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, 3:2, 2:3, 5:4, 4:5, 21:9 · gpt-image-2-5-flare/gpt-image-2-5-sunburst: 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4

count.description: Variations of this one prompt: every image gets the same prompt, so different subjects are separate calls. Up to 10 with projectId; headless caps at 1. A 2x2 or 3x3 grid in one picture is a Shot's or the prompt box's Grid (params.gridMode), not count.

referenceImageUrls.description: Headless (no projectId) nano-banana-2-1 only. With a projectId, upload via slates_upload_reference_image. Label every image role in the prompt.

referenceAssetIds.description: Project assets as references — UUIDs or badge codes ("IMG-A8"), resolved at call time. Requires projectId. Caps: nano-banana-2-1: 14 · gpt-image-2-5-flare/gpt-image-2-5-sunburst: 16 · flux-3/seedream-5-lite: 10. Label every reference role in the prompt.

background.description: Return generationId(s) now instead of blocking; poll slates_get_generation_status. Recommended for video.

confirm.description: Set true only to relay the user's explicit OK of this exact spend.

folderId.description: Folder the result lands in (slates_list_folders). Omit it to follow the folder chosen in the user's Slates window, else the project root; null is the root, on purpose. Needs projectId.

tools.name: slates_generate_video
tools.description: Generate video via Slates credits. Choose the model with slates-model-selection. Video models prompt very differently: the estimate returns the chosen model's prompting card, and its full guide (slates-prompting-kling-v3 / slates-prompting-seedance / slates-prompting-seedance-2-5 / slates-prompting-omni-flash / slates-prompting-wan-3 / slates-prompting-minimax-h3 / slates-prompting-ltx-2-5) covers modes the card leaves out, via slates_get_prompting_guide. Read slates-content-policy when the scene involves conflict, creatures, crowds, destruction, weapons, or young characters. projectId, aspectRatio, and duration are required (requires_clarification otherwise). Show the user the estimate and wait for their OK before any generation, however small. Cost above 17 credits, or any image reference (frame, ingredient, character, environment or style), also returns requires_confirm — pass confirm=true only to relay that OK. Image-to-video via firstFrameAssetId; a last frame via lastFrameAssetId and ingredients via ingredientAssetIds, each param stating which models take it. Asset params take UUIDs or badge codes ("IMG-A8").

model.description:
One of: kling-v3.0-std | kling-v3.0-pro | kling-v3.0-omni | seedance-2 | seedance-2.5 | omni-flash | wan-3.0 | kling-v4.0 | minimax-h3 | minimax-h3-max | minimax-h3-max-turbo | ltx-2-5 | ltx-2-5-pro. Pass the BASE id — duration and videoResolution are separate params (registry cost keys like "kling-v3-standard-8s" auto-resolve). All are VIDEO-only.
Seedance 2.0: THE 4K AND VALUE SEAT beside the 2.5 default — the only Seedance with native 4K (Pro-gated; base accounts get PRO_REQUIRED) and cheaper than 2.5 at every resolution they share, with the same physics, effects and scale strengths; shorter takes, fewer references, no timestamps. VIDEO-ONLY. A bare "seedance" still resolves here for older CLIs that expect 4K.
Seedance 2.5: DEFAULT VIDEO MODEL — the strongest seat for physics, effects, scale and hero shots, and the only Seedance that takes long single takes, many references, audio-only references and integer-second timestamps. No 4K, and dearer than 2.0 at every shared resolution: go to 2.0 for 4K or the same resolution cheaper. LENGTH is the price dial — quote long takes first. VIDEO-ONLY. Timestamp grammar and the edit/extend words that make the provider reclassify and fail a generation are in slates-prompting-seedance-2-5.
Kling 3.0: THE COST-EFFECTIVE SEAT — strong start-frame adherence (identity, layout, text), acting, dialogue and lip-sync; pick it when the budget matters and the shot is a performance or a start-frame animation. Kling is also the ONLY engine behind the Motion Transfer and Lip Sync tools.
Kling 4.0: The newest Kling, for single takes longer than Kling 3.0 reaches. Dearer per second and slower than 3.0, and on the same start frame 3.0 Pro won on camera and feel, so Kling 3.0 stays the Kling seat for everything else. Sound is always on at no extra cost. Start frame with an optional last frame, multi-shot sequences, or text alone; no reference images. VIDEO-ONLY.
Gemini Omni Flash 1.1: Google's video model, version 1.1 since 2026-10-17, with native synced audio in the same pass; 1080p and 4K are upscales of its 720p render. Takes a start frame with an optional last frame, or reference images plus short reference videos that carry a likeness (their audio is ignored), with no audio references. It cuts between shots by default, so ask for a single shot. Route here for cheap takes with sound and reference-driven character consistency; LTX, H3 and H3 Max Turbo cost less per second. VIDEO-ONLY. Hero-shot quality against Seedance is not yet measured.
MiniMax H3: THE AUTHORED-AUDIO SEAT — reach for H3 when the sound is part of the shot rather than a switch on it: synchronised dialogue, scene sound and an audience-only score directed as three separate layers in ONE pass, across eleven languages. Kling and Seedance treat audio as on/off. Only H3 also carries a DECLARED REFERENCE RELATIONSHIP (kept whole, partly kept, transferred, or a loose echo). VIDEO-ONLY. Its top two resolution tiers are UPSCALES of the native render, not larger generations — judge at native and upscale in post. Reference images past the fifth are a PAID key dimension: pass referenceImages when quoting.
MiniMax H3 Max: THE SPEED SEAT, dearer than base H3 at 768p and equal at 480p — never the cheap H3 and never the default. A post-train of the H3 weights: MEASURED 2026-08-27 at about 12x faster than base H3 on the same prompt and params, queue to finished file, plus a thin vendor-reported quality edge. It tops out at a 1080p refinement of its 768p render. It takes the same omni-reference set as base H3 and animates start and end frames — but not both in one call, the same as base H3: frames and references go to different endpoints. Never describe this row as taking no image or reference input. Route here when a fast turnaround on text-to-video or a start-frame shot is worth the premium.
MiniMax H3 Max Turbo: THE BUDGET SEAT of the MiniMax family: a second post-train of the H3 weights, billed at half H3 Max's rate at every tier. Its 1080p is a refinement of the native 768p render, not a native 1080p generation. INPUTS ARE FRAMES, NOT REFERENCES: text-to-video and start/end frames only, with no reference endpoint, so reference-driven consistency goes to H3 Max or base H3. Route here for drafts, volume and cheap coverage, then re-run the keeper on H3 Max or a hero seat.
Wan 3.0: Alibaba's video model, added 2026-10-17: first on Artificial Analysis text-to-video that day, at about a third of Seedance 2.5's price per second at 1080p. Long single takes, multi-shot sequences with timestamps, sound on or off. Start frame with an optional last frame, or references across images, videos and audio cited as Image N / Video N / Audio N (audio-only allowed); frames and references never mix. Reference video seconds bill on top of the output. Route here for long takes, timed multi-shot scenes and reference-driven shots on a budget; Seedance 2.5 stays the default. VIDEO-ONLY.
LTX-2.5: THE VOLUME SEAT — the cheapest native 1080p second with sound included (H3 Max Turbo's 1080p is refined from 768p), and the row for MANY takes rather than one hero shot. Native synced audio is included free at every tier, unlike Kling where sound is a paid key dimension. It reaches higher resolutions and longer takes than most seats; use the capability surface for its resolution-dependent duration limits. VIDEO-ONLY. INPUTS ARE FRAMES, NOT REFERENCES: start frame plus an optional end frame, and no reference endpoint at all — for character consistency across shots use H3 or Kling. Route here for batch coverage, long takes, and anything where the credit budget is the binding constraint.
LTX-2.5 Pro: THE FIDELITY SEAT of the LTX pair — the full diffusion build against the base row's distilled one. 🚨 IT IS NOT A SUPERSET OF THE BASE ROW, which is the opposite of every other Pro seat here: it reaches a SHORTER resolution ladder and makes SHORTER clips, and it costs more at both tiers they share. Reaching for it because the name says Pro costs more AND takes away reach. Everything else matches the base row. Route here only when a specific shot needs the fidelity and fits inside its narrower envelope.

Per model: kling-v3.0-std/kling-v3.0-omni: 720p, 4k (default 720p) · kling-v3.0-pro: 1080p, 4k (default 1080p) · seedance-2: 480p, 720p, 1080p, 4k (default 1080p) · seedance-2.5/wan-3.0: 480p, 720p, 1080p (default 720p) · omni-flash: 720p, 1080p, 4k (default 720p) · kling-v4.0: 720p, 1080p (default 720p) · minimax-h3: 480p, 768p, 2k, 4k (default 768p) · minimax-h3-max/minimax-h3-max-turbo: 480p, 768p, 1080p (default 768p) · ltx-2-5: 720p, 1080p, 1440p, 4k (default 1080p) · ltx-2-5-pro: 720p, 1080p (default 1080p). 4K video is Pro-only (the server returns PRO_REQUIRED for a base-tier account).

firstFrameAssetId.description: Starting frame for image-to-video (UUID or badge code, resolved at call time).

ingredientAssetIds.description: Visual reference / ingredient assets. Cap per model, combined across the ingredient/character/environment/style params: kling-v3.0-std/kling-v3.0-pro/kling-v3.0-omni: 4 · seedance-2/minimax-h3/minimax-h3-max: 9 · seedance-2.5: 30 · omni-flash/wan-3.0: 10 · kling-v4.0/minimax-h3-max-turbo/ltx-2-5/ltx-2-5-pro: 0 (prompt and frames only). 2-4 strong references beat both extremes.

environmentAssetIds.description: Location references — keeps a location consistent.

videoReferenceSeconds.description: DEPRECATED — the singular partner of videoReferenceSecondsEach.

audioReferenceAssetId.description: DEPRECATED — use audioReferenceAssetIds. Carries no spoken text.

videoReferenceAssetIds.description: Reference VIDEOS, cited in the prompt as "video 1", "video 2"… in the order given. seedance-2 / seedance-2.5 / omni-flash / minimax-h3 / minimax-h3-max / wan-3.0 only; per-model caps are on audioReferenceAssetIds. On Seedance and Wan 3.0, billing switches to the vref key (input+output seconds); Omni Flash caps each clip at 10s. Pass videoReferenceSecondsEach. Over the cap is REFUSED, never trimmed.

model.description:
Audio surface.
Seed Audio 1.0: DEFAULT audio model — the one-pass SCENE workhorse: dialogue, SFX and ambience together from ONE plain sentence. Route here for continuity beds, room tone, crowd and nature soundscapes, and quick scratch VO. AUDIO-ONLY. Takes one image XOR up to three audio clips as references, never both. Inworld Realtime TTS-2: THE VOICE SEAT — one named voice saying one line, billed per CHARACTER not per second. Route here when WHO is speaking matters. NOT scene audio — that is seed-audio; a single effect is eleven-sfx.

tools.name: slates_edit_video
tools.description: Edit an EXISTING video clip with one instruction — character swap, environment change, style transfer — in one pass, no masking. Original motion, camera, and audio are preserved; only what the prompt names changes. Use when a clip is ~90% right (fix it, don't re-roll it) or to AI-edit the user's own footage. Engine routing, clip-length and resolution windows are on the `model` param (subject and style refs: kling-v3.0-omni-edit and kling-v3.0-omni-pro-edit only); seedanceFace:true for AI-character faces on seedance-2.5-edit. Cost is per second: output seconds on Kling and Omni Flash, input + output on Seedance; quote it with slates_estimate_generation_cost. Subjects to swap IN go as characterAssetIds (frontal + angle images become Kling elements — Kling models only); style refs as styleAssetIds; max 4 combined. The edited clip saves as a NEW asset linked to its parent (chain edits freely). Routing: the `model` param and slates-model-selection. Prompting: slates-prompting-kling-v3 §Edit / slates-prompting-omni-flash. Show the user the estimate and wait for their OK before any generation, however small. Cost above 17 credits, or any character or style reference, also returns requires_confirm — pass confirm=true only to relay that OK.

prompt.description: The change, not the whole scene — e.g. "replace the man with @marcus", "make it a rainy night", "turn the street into a neon Tokyo alley". Mention subjects with @name; the transport compiles them to Kling's @ElementN notation (Kling models). For omni-flash-edit keep it simple and add "Keep everything else the same."

model.description:
Default kling-v3.0-omni-edit. Character and style references: Only kling-v3.0-omni-edit and kling-v3.0-omni-pro-edit take them; the other engines refuse them.
Seedance 2.5 Edit: VIDEO-TO-VIDEO EDIT via slates_edit_video, and the only edit engine that takes a clip longer than the other two reach — that length is the whole reason to route here. Inside their range, compare on fidelity instead: Omni Flash edit won the prompt-only head-to-head, and Kling edit is the one that takes reference images. Edits audio on the same row (re-voice, re-accent, translate with re-fitted lips, replace BGM). Costs about 1.2x a plain 2.5 generation of the same length: an edit bills at twice the reduced video-reference rate.
Kling O3 Video Edit: VIDEO-TO-VIDEO EDIT, the REF-DRIVEN one: it is the only edit seat that takes element/style reference images to lock subject identity, and its keepAudio preserves the original audio verbatim. Route here when an edit NEEDS reference images or bit-exact audio; for prompt-only footage-synced VFX, omni-flash-edit won the fidelity head-to-head. One instruction beat per pass — multi-beat prompts get under-executed.
Omni Flash 1.1 Edit: VIDEO-TO-VIDEO EDIT, prompt-only, on Omni Flash 1.1 since 2026-10-17. The 1.0 edit won the head-to-head against Kling edit on real talking footage (lips held, audio near-identical, both action beats landed); 1.1 has not been re-measured against it yet. Footage-synced prop, effect, environment and lighting swaps; 1080p and 4K output are upscales. Takes NO reference images — identity swaps needing refs go to Kling edit. Fidelity is EARNED by prompt discipline; the exact form is in slates-prompting-omni-flash.
Source-clip length per engine: kling-v3.0-omni-edit/kling-v3.0-omni-pro-edit: 3-15s · omni-flash-edit: 3-10s · seedance-2.5-edit: 4-30s. Output resolution: kling-v3.0-omni-edit/kling-v3.0-omni-pro-edit: 1080p only (fixed — do not pass videoResolution) · omni-flash-edit: 720p, 1080p, 4k (default 720p) · seedance-2.5-edit: 480p, 720p, 1080p (default 720p)

tools.name: slates_trim_video
tools.description: Trim a video asset to an exact [inSec, outSec] window and save the result as a NEW clip linked to the original (the original is untouched). This is the fit-to-model primitive: when a clip is longer than the edit or reference window the chosen model accepts (its `model` param and estimate state the window), trim it first, then edit the trimmed clip. Exact re-encode (not a keyframe-snapped cut) so the result honors hard duration caps to the frame; any phone rotation flag is baked into the pixels in the same pass. The new clip lands with correct duration/width/height immediately. inSec defaults to 0. Pass pieces to cut the window into SEVERAL clips in one call, as the Trim & split dialog does (split points, or Auto-split by longest piece, with seconds shared between neighbours); every new clip comes back.

assetId.description: The VIDEO asset to trim — UUID or badge code ("VID-V3", bare "V3"); resolves against the project at call time.

outSec.description: Trim end in seconds. Must be greater than inSec.

longestSec.description: Auto-split: even pieces, none longer than this (Longest piece). Use instead of splitsAtSec.

shareSec.description: Pieces share: each piece also holds this many seconds of the next (default 0), so an edit can carry on into the next clip.

pieces.description: Cut the window into several clips instead of one. Needs splitsAtSec or longestSec.

tools.name: slates_get_generation_status
tools.description: Poll one generation by id after a background=true submit. Returns status (pending/processing/completed/failed/cancelled), the error message on failure, and the finished asset record (with id, code, filePath) on completion. Pass waitSeconds 45: the call long-polls and returns the moment the generation ends, so one call replaces many quick polls, each of which re-reads your whole context. A video commonly takes a few long-poll calls. Generations survive app restarts (the desktop resumes in-flight provider jobs on boot).

tools.name: slates_export_cuts
tools.description: Start or retry a background export of existing named cuts to local files without generating media or spending credits. Version 2 selects cuts × delivery aspects from slates_get_variant_grid and returns batchId, manifestPath and frozen named outputs immediately; poll slates_get_export_batch. Version 2 with variants (a pick read through slates_get_variants grid) and items [] exports every variant of a cut's slots in every picked format in one request, adding the rows a combination lacks: one body and ten hooks in four formats is forty named files. Each variant's picture is joined from parts rendered once per format and kept, so a shared body renders once and an unchanged export again renders nothing; an output cut at a seam carries segments (parts, reused), and one that rendered whole says why. Variants requires variant-grid. Repeating the same batchId and selection reattaches or retries unfinished outputs; completed files are checked and never overwritten. Naming, delivery and provenance are frozen by the desktop. CSV contains completed MP4s only and is unverified against a live Meta import. Missing takes are reported per cut, never filled. Version 2 requires ad-variant-export; update Slates on capability refusal. Legacy directory/manifestId/items/action requests remain supported. For one cut, slates_export_video is enough.

items.description: Delivery format id from slates_get_variant_grid.formats; the desktop validates it and supplies dimensions.

taxonomy.description: Naming fields. Prefill recorded variation choices by position, never infer them from labels. The desktop owns filename formatting and collision resolution.

items.description: Required for version 2 start/retry (may be [] beside variants) and legacy start. Version 2 selects existing timelineIds with aspects/formats/taxonomy; legacy selects timelineId/format.

version.description: Use version 2 with batchId and items for delivery-format batches. Omit version for legacy directory/manifestId requests.

batchId.description: Required for version 2. Reuse this id and the same items to reattach or retry.

exportRoot.description: Optional export root; the desktop remembers it and creates a fresh batch folder.

timelineId.description: The cut with the slots, or any timeline of its family.

picks.description: Slot id to the alternative ids picked in it; a slot left out takes all its alternatives.

items.description: Delivery format id from slates_get_variant_grid.formats; the desktop validates it and supplies dimensions.

aspects.description: Delivery format ids; default the cut's own formats, else master.

variants.description: A grid pick to export: each combination gets a variant row if it has none, and every variant exports in every format, beside any items. Requires variant-grid.

Returns receipts and per-output states immediately through GET, including after a desktop restart. Never starts or retries a render and never spends credits.
