Completed files and frozen names remain available for retry with slates_export_cuts. Never generates media or spends credits. Requires ad-variant-export; update Slates on capability refusal.

tools.name: slates_get_variant_grid
tools.description: Read the variant grid of existing named cuts, recorded slot choices, missing takes and delivery format ids with actual dimensions. Shows absent combinations without creating them; missing-take prices are local quotes, never generation requests. Select existing timelineIds and returned aspects for slates_export_cuts. For a cut's slots (hooks, body, end card) crossed with formats, read slates_get_variants with grid. Requires ad-variant-export; update Slates on capability refusal.

tools.name: slates_get_variants
tools.description: Read a cut's ad variants: hooks, a shared body and an end card as slots laid end to end, each slot's alternatives (each a timeline: sequenceId, its length), and the variant rows, one alternative per slot, each built into an ordinary timeline (cutId) with its seams (J-cut, L-cut, crossfade or cut, who picked it and why, and what the media held back) and its state: current, edited by hand and left alone, or unbuilt, with behind once its sources changed since its timeline was built. The cut's own lanes are the bed under every variant. Any timeline of the family answers: the cut, a slot's sequence or a variant's timeline. With grid, it adds the grid for a pick of alternatives per slot and of delivery formats: each combination (name, variantId and cutId, null when no row has it yet), files (combinations × formats), the formats offered with their sizes, and missingTakes (shotIds of intended takes the picked alternatives lack; credits, what making them bills in all, the figure to quote; costs, dollars per take request; both null when unpriceable; the grid never generates). Export that pick with slates_export_cuts variants. Reading writes nothing: a behind variant catches up when its timeline is opened (slates_get_timeline) or exported, after any slates_edit_variant_slots or slates_edit_variants call, and on rebuild, which also drops hand edits. Requires ad-variants; update Slates on capability refusal.

picks.description: Slot id to the alternative ids picked in it; a slot left out takes all its alternatives.

items.description: Delivery format id from slates_get_variant_grid.formats; the desktop validates it and supplies dimensions.

aspects.description: Delivery format ids; default the cut's own formats, else master.

grid.description: Add the grid for this pick: {} for every alternative in the cut's formats. Requires variant-grid.

tools.name: slates_edit_variant_slots
tools.description: Add, rename, move or remove a cut's ad-variant slots (hook, body, end card: names, never types) and their alternatives, as the Ad variants view in the Inspector does. add-alternative with clipIds collapses those clips off the cut into a new nested sequence, so the body exists once and a fix to it shows in every variant; the first slot made from clips, or one named Body, anchors the bed where its clips sat. Without clipIds or sequenceId it makes an empty sequence to fill with slates_add_clip_to_timeline (its sequenceId is the timelineId). Removing an alternative also removes the variant rows that pick it (removedVariantIds), each with its timeline unless edited by hand; removing a slot drops each row's pick for it. A removed slot's or alternative's own sequence stays, as an ordinary cut. Every unedited variant rebuilds after. Returns the whole set as slates_get_variants does, with the new slotId or alternativeId. Requires ad-variants; update Slates on capability refusal.

timelineId.description: The cut: for add, and for add-alternative with slotName instead of slotId.

slotName.description: add-alternative without slotId: makes this slot first.

name.description: A slot's or an alternative's name. Defaults: Hook, Body, End card; '<slot> 1'.

at.description: add: the position among the slots.

orderIndex.description: update or update-alternative: move it to this position.

bedFrame.description: update: the bed frame this slot's first frame meets in every variant (one slot per cut); null clears it.

clipIds.description: add-alternative: move these clips (and their linked sound) off the cut into a new sequence; what stays is the bed.

sequenceId.description: add-alternative: an existing timeline of this project to hold as it is.

tools.name: slates_edit_variants
tools.description: Add, change, rebuild or remove ad variant rows on a cut's slots, as the Ad variants view does. Each row picks one alternative per slot and is built into an ordinary timeline (cutId), named for ad export, ready for slates_export_cuts. Seams: the picture always cuts where slots meet; the sound is picked from the transcripts (L-cut when the outgoing line runs past its picture, J-cut when the next slot opens on speech, a short crossfade when both sides have sound on audio lanes, else a cut, a picture cut over the bed with no dialogue), or set by hand per seam; either way held to the media past the cut, with the reason in the result. A row's timeline catches up with its sources when opened, exported or after any slot or row action, unless edited by hand; rebuild takes the sources and drops the hand edits. remove deletes the row and its timeline unless edited by hand. Returns the whole set and the new variantIds. Requires ad-variants; update Slates on capability refusal.

timelineId.description: add: the cut with the slots.

combinations.description: add: one row per combination of the slots' alternatives not already a row.

choices.description: Slot id to alternative id. A slot left out plays its first alternative.

additionalProperties.description: 'auto' for the automatic pick, { kind: 'cut' }, or { kind, frames } with frames 1 to 600: j (the next slot's sound leads by frames), l (this slot's sound runs on), crossfade (its length).

seams.description: Keyed by the slot AFTER the seam.

rows.description: add: the rows to add; omit for one row of first alternatives.

name.description: update: the row and its timeline take it.

additionalProperties.description: 'auto' for the automatic pick, { kind: 'cut' }, or { kind, frames } with frames 1 to 600: j (the next slot's sound leads by frames), l (this slot's sound runs on), crossfade (its length).

seams.description: update: merged; 'auto' gives a seam back to the automatic pick.

tools.name: slates_get_recipe
tools.description: Find what made an exported ad from its recipe ID, its full ad name or its file name (anything holding __r-<id>). Returns every export that carried the recipe (batch, export time, ad name, files per format, the timeline id and name, its taxonomy); then each clip with its timing and asset and, when generated, the model, prompt, references and key settings frozen at export, and the Shot and board it came from (Shot, board and asset names and labels are read as they are now, not frozen); then any timeline that still renders the recipe. Searches every project unless projectId is given. When nothing matches, notFound says why: exported before ad names carried a recipe ID, or the timeline changed and its export folder is unreachable. Read-only; never generates or spends. Requires recipe-lookup; update Slates on capability refusal.

recipe.description: The recipe ID (the characters after __r-), or a whole ad name, file name or path containing __r-<id>.

projectId.description: Search only this project; omit to search every project.

tools.name: slates_reframe_clip
tools.description: Set or reset a clip framing override for one delivery aspect and return the desktop computed framing report. Changes focus, fill/fit and zoom without duplicating the timeline or generating media. follow: "face" makes a vertical cut follow a talking head (framing, when sent too, lands first) and answers follow: the clip keyframes, samples, found, still and the lost spans in seconds. Requires ad-variant-export, and reframe-follow for follow; update Slates on capability refusal.

aspect.description: Delivery format id from slates_get_variant_grid.formats; the desktop validates it and supplies dimensions.

framing.description: Normalized focus and zoom for this clip/aspect. Null resets the override; the desktop binds it to the current take. Required unless follow is set.

follow.description: "face" finds the face in the clip and keys its focusX/focusY to it (smooth, held where the face is lost; every format draws those keys, each keyframe editable by hand or with slates_set_clip_keyframes); "off" removes those keys. Runs on the computer and spends nothing.

tools.name: slates_get_reframe_report
tools.description: Inspect effective delivery framing, computed dimensions, kept frame percentage, upscale and stale-take or missing-media warnings for a cut or one clip. Read before reframing; warnings never trigger generation or disable export. Requires ad-variant-export; update Slates on capability refusal.

aspect.description: Delivery format id from slates_get_variant_grid.formats; the desktop validates it and supplies dimensions.

tools.name: slates_get_timeline
tools.description: Get (or lazily create) a named editing timeline, or the stable legacy default when timelineId is omitted, with all tracks, clips, markers, and a flat clipIndex mapping every clip back to its source asset (assetId + code + label). Frames are the unit of time; durationSec is provided. Call this before adding, reordering, or removing clips, and before exporting — it tells you the timeline id, frame rate, resolution, and current end frame.

tools.name: slates_get_timeline_loudness
tools.description: Measure a timeline's loudness as its export writes it: integrated LUFS (gated, ITU-R BS.1770), loudness range (LRA, LU), true peak (dBTP, read 4x oversampled) and sample peak of the whole mix, the same for each lane alone (every other lane muted), and a short-term (3 s) and momentary (400 ms) reading per second in `mix.trace`. Read-only: the desktop renders the sound to a temporary file and measures it; nothing is saved and nothing is spent. Check a mix against its bar before exporting: a short for social is -14 LUFS integrated with a true peak of -1 dBTP or under (`target` in the answer, shown, never enforced). To move the integrated level by D dB, multiply masterVolume by 10^(D/20) with slates_update_timeline_settings, then measure again and check the true peak. fromSec and toSec measure one span alone; trackId reads one lane. Null means silence, or a span too short (range and short-term need 3 s). Same numbers as the Output level popover's Measure. Requires the desktop's loudness capability; update Slates on refusal.

timelineId.description: The cut to measure; absent: the project's default timeline.

fromSec.description: Measure from here (timeline seconds), as if the span were exported alone.

toSec.description: Measure to here (timeline seconds); absent: the end.

trackId.description: Read this one lane alone (with the mix); absent: every lane heard.

tools.name: slates_add_clip_to_timeline
tools.description: Append a video or audio asset from the project to the project's timeline (or place it at an explicit startFrame). Defaults match the desktop UI: video clips go to the end of the first video track; audio clips (music, voiceover, AI audio) go after the last clip on the first AUDIO track and are mixed under the video on export. An empty timeline auto-adopts the first video clip's resolution and frame rate; later higher-resolution clips raise the canvas. Overlapping video clips resolve top-track-wins. Optionally trim with sourceInFrame/sourceOutFrame (frames at the SOURCE fps). An audio asset may instead take startSec, sourceInSec and sourceOutSec (or sourceInSample/sourceOutSample) to the sample, for a music edit between frames; with no startSec it starts where the lane's last sound ends, so clips appended in turn butt exactly. Use slates_get_timeline first to see current clips and pick positions. To lay a board's chosen clips in board order, use slates_edit_cut (build) instead.

assetId.description: Video or audio asset already in the project.

trackId.description: Target track (type must match the asset: video asset → video track, audio asset → audio track). Default: the first track of the matching type.

startFrame.description: Timeline frame to place the clip at. Default: append after the last clip.

startSec.description: Audio lane: where its sound starts on the timeline, in seconds to the sample; it may fall between frames.

sourceInSec.description: Audio lane: where in its file the sound starts, in seconds, to the sample.

sourceOutSec.description: Audio lane: where in its file the sound ends, in seconds, to the sample.

sourceInSample.description: The media in as a sample count at 48000 Hz, instead of sourceInSec.

sourceOutSample.description: The media out as a sample count at 48000 Hz, instead of sourceOutSec.

tools.name: slates_reorder_clips
tools.description: Reorder the clips on one timeline track. Pass the COMPLETE list of the track's clip ids in the desired playback order; clips are repacked back-to-back from frame 0 (existing gaps are removed). Get current clip ids from slates_get_timeline.

tools.name: slates_remove_clip
tools.description: Remove a clip from the timeline (the source asset is untouched). By default it leaves a gap at the clip's old position, which MP4 export renders as black. ripple: true closes the gap instead: the lane's later clips move left by the clip's length (needs projectId). An overlay track's text and image clips keep their times, and the gap is just no overlay.

ripple.description: Close the gap: the lane's later clips move up. Needs projectId.

tools.name: slates_edit_timeline_clips
tools.description: Trim, roll, ripple, slip, move or split clips on the timeline, as the Cut's tools do; the source files are untouched (to cut a new file, use slates_trim_video). trim moves one edge (edge, then frame or deltaFrames): mode overwrite (default) covers a neighbour it grows into, ripple moves the lane's later clips by the change, roll moves the cut shared with the clip that meets this edge. A trim cuts media and never changes speed. slip changes which part of the media a clip shows without moving it (deltaFrames in timeline frames, or deltaSourceFrames in the file's). move takes clipId or clipIds, keeps their spacing, to startFrame or by deltaFrames, optionally onto trackId (a lane of the same type); mode overwrite cuts what they land on, insert pushes the lane's later clips right (a landing inside a clip moves to its nearer edge). split cuts at frame (or sec) every clip under it on the timeline, or only clipIds. Returns the clips it wrote as they now stand, the ids it deleted, the cut's durationFrames and any staleTransitions (whose clips no longer meet); a refused edit says why.

clipIds.description: move or split: several clips of one timeline.

frame.description: trim: where the edge goes. split: where to cut. Timeline frames.

sec.description: split: where to cut, in seconds.

deltaFrames.description: trim, slip or move: how far, in timeline frames; negative is left (slip: earlier media).

deltaSourceFrames.description: slip: how far, in the file's own frames.

startFrame.description: move: where the first clip lands.

trackId.description: move: another lane of the same type.

timelineId.description: split without clipIds: a named cut; omit for the project's timeline.

mode.description: trim: overwrite, ripple or roll. move: overwrite or insert.

tools.name: slates_update_clip
tools.description: Set a timeline clip's own speed, volume, split edit (J-cut or L-cut) and fades, as the Cut's Inspector does. Only the fields you name change; null puts one back to the default. speed keeps the clip's media in and out points and its start and changes its length (2 is twice as fast, half as long); with ripple: true the lane's later clips move by the change, otherwise a longer clip covers what follows. audioOffsetFrames, on a video clip, moves its own sound against its picture in sync: below 0 is a J-cut (the sound starts first), above 0 an L-cut (it runs on). Fades are frames: fadeIn/fadeOut for the picture, audioFadeIn/audioFadeOut for the sound. volume is linear gain (1 = 0 dB, 0 = silent). look, on a clip with a picture, is the Inspector's Blend, Grain and Colour, sent whole: blend mixes the picture with what is under it (multiply darkens, screen lightens, overlay and soft-light add contrast), grain is film grain from 0 to 1, saturation is colour from 0 (black and white) through 1 (as shot) to 2; null clears the look. effects is the clip's sound effects, sent whole, in order: a volume (gain in dB) and an eq (its low-pass), each fixed or keyed in frames from the clip's start, the same in preview and export. speedRamp keys the speed over the clip (a slow-motion ramp): media in and out stay, the length becomes what the keys take, and the sound follows tape-style; not with speed. speedSound 'tape' makes a constant speed's sound change pitch with it. On an audio lane, startSec, sourceInSec and sourceOutSec (or sourceInSample and sourceOutSample) set where its sound starts and its media in and out to the sample, for a music edit between frames; a longer clip covers what follows unless ripple; not with speed in the same call.

speed.description: 1 is normal speed; null is too, at the natural length of the clip.

volume.description: Linear gain under the lane fader; 1 is unchanged.

audioOffsetFrames.description: Video clips: the split edit, in timeline frames.

look.description: The whole look, at least one field; a field left out is its default (normal, no grain, colour 1). null clears it.

id.description: Kept when sent back; a new effect gets one.

type.description: volume: gain in dB (param gainDb, -60 silent to +12). eq: its low-pass (params 'lowpass.frequency' in Hz, 20 to 20000, swept by octave; 'lowpass.q', 0.1 to 10, 0.71 flat).

frame.description: Frames from the clip's start, at the timeline's frame rate; may fall between frames, read at that exact time (110.4 is 4.6 s at 24 fps).

easing.description: The curve from this key to the next. Default linear; hold jumps at the next key.

keyframes.description: Keys by parameter name; a keyed parameter reads its keys instead of its fixed value.

effects.description: A clip with sound: its effect list, sent whole; null clears it. A split picture's go to its sound clip.

frame.description: Frames from the clip's start, at the timeline's frame rate; may fall between frames, read at that exact time (110.4 is 4.6 s at 24 fps).

easing.description: The curve from this key to the next. Default linear; hold jumps at the next key.

speedRamp.description: Speeds (0.05 to 20) keyed in frames from the clip's start; null goes back to one speed. Its linked sound follows.

speedSound.description: How a constant speed's sound plays: tape moves pitch with speed; keep-pitch (or null) holds it. A ramp's is always tape.

ripple.description: With speed, speedRamp or a sound clip's new media out: move the lane's later clips instead of covering them.

startSec.description: Audio lane: where its sound starts on the timeline, in seconds to the sample; it may fall between frames.

sourceInSec.description: Audio lane: where in its file the sound starts, in seconds, to the sample.

sourceOutSec.description: Audio lane: where in its file the sound ends, in seconds, to the sample.

sourceInSample.description: The media in as a sample count at 48000 Hz, instead of sourceInSec.

sourceOutSample.description: The media out as a sample count at 48000 Hz, instead of sourceOutSec.

tools.name: slates_add_transition
tools.description: Put a transition (dissolve, wipe, crossfade and the other kinds) on a cut between two clips that meet on one lane, as the Cut's clip menu does. Name the cut by fromClipId and toClipId, or by one clipId and side ('end' runs this clip into the next, 'start' the last clip into this one). A cut holds one transition, so adding where one exists changes it. It never refuses short media: the result's shortHandles says how many frames are missing and offers the fixes (slates_update_transition fix: freeze or shorten). On an audio lane, durationMs sets a crossfade to the millisecond and curve how the sounds cross: a 10 ms linear crossfade with alignment 'end' joins two cuts of one song as a triangular crossfade does. For a fade to or from black, set the clip's fades with slates_update_clip instead. The open Cut shows the change.

clipId.description: One clip of the cut, with side.

kind.description: A kind from slates_get_timeline's transitionKinds for this lane: picture kinds on video and overlay lanes, sound kinds on audio lanes. Default: a dissolve, or a crossfade on sound.

durationFrames.description: How long it lasts, in timeline frames. Default 0.5 s, shortened to what the clips allow; a length you name that is too long is refused with the longest that fits.

alignment.description: center (default) straddles the cut; start begins at the cut; end finishes at it.

params.description: The kind's settings. freeze: true holds the edge frame where the media runs short. On a picture transition, audio: false stops the clips' sound crossfading with it.

durationMs.description: Audio lane: the crossfade's length in milliseconds (1 to 10000), placed to the sample, so it may be shorter than a frame. Instead of durationFrames or durationSec.

curve.description: Audio lane: 'equal-power' (default) for two different sounds, 'linear' (straight lines, a triangular crossfade) for a join inside one piece of music.

tools.name: slates_update_transition
tools.description: Change a transition's kind, length, alignment or settings by its id (slates_get_timeline lists them under transitions), or apply one of the two fixes for short media: fix 'freeze' holds the edge frame for the missing frames, fix 'shorten' cuts it to the longest the media covers. Only the fields you name change; on an audio lane durationMs and curve set a crossfade to the millisecond, and a length in frames or seconds replaces one in milliseconds. Returns the transition with its span (durationSec, curve) and any frames still missing.

fix.description: Instead of other fields: the short-media fix.

kind.description: A kind from slates_get_timeline's transitionKinds for this lane: picture kinds on video and overlay lanes, sound kinds on audio lanes. Default: a dissolve, or a crossfade on sound.

durationFrames.description: How long it lasts, in timeline frames. Default 0.5 s, shortened to what the clips allow; a length you name that is too long is refused with the longest that fits.

alignment.description: center (default) straddles the cut; start begins at the cut; end finishes at it.

params.description: The kind's settings. freeze: true holds the edge frame where the media runs short. On a picture transition, audio: false stops the clips' sound crossfading with it.

durationMs.description: Audio lane: the crossfade's length in milliseconds (1 to 10000), placed to the sample, so it may be shorter than a frame. Instead of durationFrames or durationSec.

curve.description: Audio lane: 'equal-power' (default) for two different sounds, 'linear' (straight lines, a triangular crossfade) for a join inside one piece of music.

tools.description: Take a transition off its cut, leaving a plain cut; the clips are untouched. The id is in slates_get_timeline under transitions.

tools.name: slates_manage_timeline_marker
tools.description: Add, change or delete a marker on the timeline, as the Cut's ruler and marker menus do (slates_get_timeline lists them under timeline.markers). create: frame, optional name and color. update: markerId plus any of frame, name, color. delete: markerId. The color is one of the app's marker colours by name (e.g. Red); any other is refused with the list. The open Cut shows the change.

timelineId.description: A named cut; omit for the project's timeline.

frame.description: Where the marker sits, in timeline frames.

tools.name: slates_add_timeline_track
tools.description: Add a track to the project's timeline (default: an audio track, for layering voiceover + music + AI audio). A video or audio track is appended below the existing tracks; an overlay track, for text and image overlays, goes on top so it draws over every other track. Returns the new track and the full timeline.

type.description: Default: audio. overlay needs a desktop with text and image overlays.

tools.name: slates_add_text_clip
tools.description: Put text on the timeline: captions, a headline, a keyword, a call to action, a title-card label, a logo with words. Each item is one text clip on an overlay track, drawn over the video in preview and export; a batch lands in one transaction, all or none. Captions that follow the voice: one clip per line, with each word's timing in words. Set a label exactly with font (a font Slates carries) and fontSize (a fraction of the frame's height); it then centres the middle of its capitals on x, y. pictureAssetId draws an image before the words; clips sharing a line name are set side by side and centred as one, so a logo strip such as 'Blender + slates' is three items in one line (needs text-fonts; update Slates on refusal). Read slates_get_timeline first for the frame rate, where clips sit and textFonts. Returns the clips and the timeline. Change one later with slates_update_overlay_clip, remove it with slates_remove_clip.

words.description: Word timings in timeline seconds, for captions that follow the voice; each word's end comes after its start.

style.description: Default: subtitle. word-pop lights up the spoken word when the clip has words.

y.description: The centre's distance from the top edge, as a fraction of the frame's height.

startFrame.description: Where the clip starts, in timeline frames.

durationSec.description: How long it shows, in seconds. Default: 3.

endFrame.description: The frame it ends before, instead of durationSec.

trackId.description: An overlay track (slates_add_timeline_track, type overlay). Default: the topmost unlocked, shown overlay track with room, or a new one on top.

Each item is one image clip on an overlay track, drawn in preview and export; a batch lands in one transaction, all or none. The picture is an image asset already in the project. Returns the clips and the timeline. Change one later with slates_update_overlay_clip, remove it with slates_remove_clip.

tools.description: Change a text clip's words or look, or an image overlay's place, size and opacity. Only the fields you name change; null puts one back to the style's or the default. tools.name: slates_set_clip_keyframes
tools.description: Animate or set a timeline clip's transform with keyframes: a punch-in, a slow push, a Ken Burns move, a slide, a spin, a fade, a crop. Each property you name gets exactly the keys you send ([] clears it back to its static value); properties you leave out keep theirs, and all of them land in one transaction. One key holds a value for the whole clip. Frames count from the clip's start and may fall between frames (110.4), read at that exact time. Units: positionX/positionY move the picture's centre in frame widths/heights (0.1 = a tenth of the frame right or down, -4..4); scale multiplies the framed size about the frame's centre (1 = as framed, 0.01..20); rotation is degrees clockwise; opacity 0..1; cropLeft/Top/Right/Bottom remove that fraction of the source from its side (0..0.99); focusX/focusY (0..1) and zoom (1..20) animate the clip's reframe for the aspect being exported. Drawn by the Cut's monitor and its export alike, both the timeline engine. Returns the clip's keys; slates_get_timeline lists every clip's keys in timeline.keyframes. Requires timeline-keyframes; update Slates on capability refusal.

tools.name: slates_add_captions
tools.description: Caption the speech in a cut: one text clip per phrase on an overlay track, each carrying its words so the spoken word lights up on the frame it is said. Free; any transcription it needs runs on the user's machine. source transcript (the default) uses the words heard in each clip, aligned to within a frame, transcribing first when needed; script spreads the clip's Shot line over the speech, with estimated timing; words takes your own timed words in timeline seconds. By default every clip with sound is captioned on a new Captions track on top. Phrases follow the caption rules unless you pass your own; tiers mark emphasis per word. The result lists mismatches, where what was heard differs from the Shot's written line (the caption shows what was said: fix the line or the captions), and skipped clips with the reason. Craft: slates_get_prompting_guide (topic: slates-captions). Change a text caption later with slates_update_overlay_clip, and a component or html caption layer with slates_update_html_clip.

Words count across the whole call in timeline order, and only those inside each clip's in and out points: a trimmed clip's earlier words are not counted (see slates-captions).

Drawn only by components: caption-editorial-emphasis sets italic and emphasis (slam draws as emphasis); kinetic-slam, clip-wipe, particle-burst, neon-glow and neon-accent colour emphasis and slam words as keywords. The text styles show regular.

Pass your own html, or block with the name of a registry block (slates_list_motion_blocks) and its variables; html with block replaces the block's document and keeps its files. It loads the project's own pictures, SVGs, fonts, stylesheets and scripts by their path in the project's folder (images/logo.svg, fonts/Brand.woff2, css/brand.css, js/library.js; the folder is projectsFolder from slates_get_app_settings, then the project id) and no other file; an export fails, naming the font, when a declared font does not load. Slates' composition check runs before the clip lands and its findings come back here: fix every error with slates_update_html_clip before moving on. Keep a transparent foreground and a background plate on separate tracks. Free. Read slates_get_timeline first for the frame rate and where clips sit. Craft: slates_get_prompting_guide (topic: slates-motion).

tools.description: Update a timeline's output settings: resolution, frame rate (24/30/60; all clips are conformed to it on export), masterVolume, or delivery formats, naming taxonomy and explicit variant grid bindings. Delivery-only updates on an explicit timeline return the computed formats. masterVolume is the output fader (linear gain: 0 is silent, 1 is unity, 4 is the maximum boost) applied to the preview and the final mix; use it to prevent clipping when stacking loud tracks. These are normally auto-managed: the first video clip sets fps and resolution, higher-res clips raise the canvas, and delivery preserves the master aspect. tools.name: slates_export_video
tools.description: Render the project's timeline to an MP4 file on disk through the desktop app's timeline engine, the renderer its monitor shows, so the file matches the preview (H.264 + AAC, every video lane composited with its transitions, fades and keyframes, gaps rendered as black; the Slates window must be open). No dialogs — pass an absolute outputPath ending in .mp4. Fails if the file exists unless overwrite=true. Blocks until encoding finishes (can take minutes for long timelines) and returns the real file size and probed duration. After success, consider slates_reveal_file to show the file to the user. Requires at least one video clip on the timeline. The sound is AAC at the timeline's Sound bitrate (slates_update_timeline_settings audioBitrate; default 320 kb/s) unless audioBitrate names one for this file. Pass exactly one of projectId (the project's default timeline) or timelineId (a named cut).

Use this for DaVinci Resolve or Premiere; current Final Cut Pro requires FCPXML, which this tool does not export. Pass an absolute outputPath ending in .xml; fails if the file exists unless overwrite=true. Pass exactly one of projectId (the project's default timeline) or timelineId (a named cut).

Each item carries `mention` — exactly what to type in a prompt to attach it (a bare name is prose and attaches nothing) — plus its image, source and voice asset ids.

tools.name: slates_create_library_item
tools.description: Save a reference to the Library in one of the project's categories (ids from slates_list_library) — a person, a location, a product, a prop, a look. Names share ONE namespace per sigil: a name whose handle is already taken comes back suffixed ("Candle 2"), so read `mention` from the result instead of assuming it. Pass imageAssetId (UUID or badge code) to bind its picture in the same call.

style.description: Optional free-text style instruction the sheet tools read.

imageAssetId.description: The one image a mention attaches. UUID or badge code ("IMG-A8").

tools.name: slates_update_library_item
tools.description: Update a Library item: rename it, move it to another category (categoryId), bind its picture (imageAssetId) or its voice (voiceAssetId, an audio asset; a thing in a location category composes as an environment and carries none). null clears an asset; the asset itself stays. Moving between a 'thing' and a 'look' category flips the sigil (@ ↔ #), and moving a thing into or out of a 'location'-template category changes what it composes as. A rename changes its handle. In every case each saved Shot that mentions the item is rewritten to match (the mention in its prompt, and its mention id), and the result's `move` reports `shotsMentioning`, `shotsRetagged` and the old and new `mention`: tell the user what changed. Pass retagShots:false to leave Shots alone; they then show the item as missing until it is mentioned again. Moving it back, or renaming it back, undoes the rewrite. extraAssetIds sets the item's extra pictures (the whole ordered list; [] clears; a mention still sends only its picture) and palette its colours (up to six; [] clears; shown and read, never sent to a model).

projectId.description: The project the item is in — asset codes resolve against it.

retagShots.description: Only with categoryId or name. Default true: Shots that mention the item follow a move or a rename that changes how it is mentioned.

imageAssetId.description: UUID or badge code; null clears.

voiceAssetId.description: An AUDIO asset, UUID or badge code; null detaches.

extraAssetIds.description: More pictures of it, in order: UUIDs or badge codes of pictures in this project. [] clears.

palette.description: Its colours: #rrggbb, #rgb or rgb(r, g, b). [] clears.

tools.name: slates_manage_library_category
tools.description: Create, rename, change what it is (set-behaviour), reorder or delete a Library category. Categories are the USER's labels ("Products", "Mascots"); never invent ones they did not ask for. create: projectId + name + kind ('thing' = used as @name in prompts, 'look' = used as #name), optional template ('person' | 'location'; the app asks "Is this a subject, a place, or a look?" — a 'location' category's things compose as environments and carry no voice; every other thing composes as a character). set-behaviour: categoryId + kind + template (null for no template); retagShots defaults to true and rewrites affected shot mentions to match. The result reports affected items and rewritten shots. rename: categoryId + name. reorder: projectId + orderedIds (every category id, in the new order). delete: categoryId — refused while the category holds items.

name.description: Up to 40 characters, as the app's name field.

tools.name: slates_copy_library_item_to_project

The original is untouched. Use this to reuse a character or product across projects; use slates_move_entity_to_project to take it out of this one instead.

tools.name: slates_get_template
tools.description: Read a Slates template file without changing anything. With `path`: what it holds (scenes, shots, library items, the models its shots are set to) and its SWAP SLOTS — every Library item (`item:i1`, labelled with its mention, e.g. @candle, with `extras` (its count of extra pictures) and `palette`) and every directly attached reference (`asset:a3`, with its roles) that slates_import_template can point at one of the project's own assets instead. Without `path`: the templates in the user's templates folder, plus any starter templates the app ships.

path.description: Absolute path of a .slatestemplate file. Omit to list saved templates.

tools.name: slates_export_template
tools.description: Save a board, a scene or one Shot as a template file someone else can start from. Give exactly one of storyboardId, sceneId or shotId. The file carries each Shot's full recipe (prompt, model, settings, reference roles, script words) plus the reference files and the Library items the Shots mention, each with its picture, extra pictures and colours; it carries no takes. The project is untouched. A file saved outside the user's templates folder is not in the template list (slates_get_template without path); the user opens it with Open a file. Returns the path, the counts and a warning for any reference whose file is missing.

path.description: Absolute path to write, ending in .slatestemplate. Its folder is created if needed.

name.description: The template's name. Defaults to the board's, scene's or Shot's.

tools.name: slates_import_template
tools.description: Add a template to a project. A board template becomes a new board; a scene template becomes a new scene of `storyboardId` (default: the most recently edited board); a single-Shot template is filed like any new Shot (into `sceneId` when given, else the last scene of `storyboardId` or of the most recently edited board). Its reference files become new assets of this project and its Library items are created here (a taken name is suffixed and the imported prompts are rewritten to match; see `renamed`). `swaps` maps a slot key from slates_get_template to an asset of THIS project (id or code) of the slot's type: the item takes that picture, or every Shot that attached the template's reference attaches it instead, and the template's own file for that slot is not imported. Generates nothing and spends nothing: price and fire the returned shotIds with slates_generate_from_shots, after the user approves the prices.

sceneIndices.description: Import only these scene indices from the inspected parts, preserving their order. Omit for the whole template.

swaps.description: { "item:i1": "IMG-A12", "asset:a3": "<asset id>" }. An item swap also leaves out the template's extra pictures and colours for it.

useTemplateCategories.description: Remove the project's untouched default Library categories the template does not use. Only acts on a project whose Library is empty; defaults to true on a project with no board.

tools.name: slates_get_reference_breakdown
tools.description: Read a reference ad's cuts and words without changing anything: each cut's start, end and seconds, the words heard in it, and the reference's size, frame rate and form (a still, no voice, soft cuts). When slates_break_down_reference already saved this asset's frames, they come back too (framesSaved: true, each cut's keyframeCode and compositeCode, the first and last frame side by side); otherwise there are no pictures and the words are the stored transcript only. Free; writes nothing. To start from a reference, read it here, then break it down.

assetId.description: The reference video or picture in the project: its code (VID-V3) or id.

tools.name: slates_break_down_reference
tools.description: Start from a reference ad: break a finished video into a new board with one Shot per cut, as the clip's Break down into shots command does, so the user can remake it with their own product. Each Shot is postered with its cut's keyframe (a poster only, never a reference or first frame), named by its seconds in the reference, and holds the words heard in that cut on the Script page. Nothing is generated and nothing spends: the result carries the board's quote, the Shot codes and each timing gap in words (a cut shorter than the model's shortest length). Local and free; the first transcription can take minutes. Name the reference by assetId, filePath or url, one of them: a url is fetched into the project's Media first, and works for a Meta Ad Library ad link (facebook.com/ads/library/?id=...) or a direct link to a video file; TikTok Creative Center, YouTube and TikTok post links are refused with the reason (download the video, then pass filePath). The result's source names the link, its kind and the video file it fetched. build false saves each cut's keyframe and first-and-last composite to a frames folder and returns the cuts, without a board: look at them with slates_get_asset_image, then call again with build (the frames are reused) and `cuts` (each cut's description, written for the user's product, becomes its Shot's prompt; onScreenText becomes a direction line), `sections` (headings) and `roles` (who or what recurs; itemId points the role at the user's own Library item). A still becomes one Shot. Generate only after the user approves the quote (slates_generate_from_shots). To be able to stop a run, name it with jobId; cancel true with that jobId (and projectId, nothing else) stops it at its next step, removing its frames and any video it fetched, until its board build starts (too late then: the board is kept).

assetId.description: A video or picture already in the project: its code (VID-V3) or id. Give this, filePath or url.

filePath.description: An absolute path to a video or picture on this computer; it is imported first.

url.description: A link to the reference: a Meta Ad Library ad or a direct video file link, fetched and imported first. Creative Center and post links are refused with the reason.

build.description: false: save the frames and return the cuts, with no board. Default true.

transcribe.description: Hear the words when no transcript is stored. Default true.

name.description: The board's name. Defaults to the reference's.

model.description: A video model id for every Shot; defaults to the app's default video model.

index.description: The cut's index from the breakdown's segments.

description.description: What this Shot shows, for the user's product: its prompt.

onScreenText.description: Words on screen in this cut, kept as a direction line, never sent as action.

sections.description: Headings on the Script page, each before the cut it starts at (hook, problem, offer...).

itemId.description: A Library item of this project (slates_list_library) to use for the role.

cuts.description: The cut indices the role appears in.

roles.description: Who or what recurs. Without itemId a role becomes a new Library item to fill in.

jobId.description: A name for this run, so a later call with cancel can stop it.

cancel.description: true: stop the run named by jobId instead of starting one.

tools.name: slates_get_product_page
tools.description: Read a product page without changing anything: the product's name, description, brand, slogan, price, pictures, logo candidates, the brand's declared colours and the page's bullet points, each with where it came from (json-ld product data, a Shopify store's product data, open-graph sharing tags, other meta tags, or the page's own pictures by size), plus notes on what the page lacks. The desktop fetches the page itself (public addresses only, no browser, nothing signed in). A page that builds itself with JavaScript, an ad library link, a post, or a link to a picture or video file is refused with the reason. Free; writes nothing. Read here first when the user names a product page, then make the product with slates_import_product.

url.description: The product page, such as a shop's /products/... page.

tools.name: slates_import_product
tools.description: Add a product to the Library from its page, as the app's Add as product does: the product becomes a thing (in Products, or the things categoryId given) with the page's first picture as its picture, the next ones as its extra pictures and the page's bullet points, price and link as its notes; its brand becomes a look with the brand's logo as its picture and the page's and logo's colours as its palette. A look of the same name already in the Library is filled in where empty, never overwritten. Pictures land in a Media folder named after the product. Give url, filePaths (absolute paths to pictures on this computer, the product's first), or both. html is the page's HTML when you already have it (a page that builds itself with JavaScript, read in your own browser); url still names the page and its pictures are still fetched. itemId fills a thing already in the Library instead of making a product, as the card's Fill from the copied product page… does: the page's pictures go after its extra pictures (the first becomes its picture when it has none; a picture it holds is not added twice), its notes are filled only when empty, and its name and category stay; not with categoryId or name. Free; nothing is generated. The result gives the product and the brand with their mention (@name, #name) for prompts and for slates_break_down_reference roles (itemId), each picture and where it came from, each picture left out with its reason, and notes on what the page lacked.

html.description: The page's HTML, read instead of fetching the page. Needs url.

filePaths.description: Absolute paths to pictures of the product on this computer, first in the order given.

name.description: The product's name. Defaults to the page's, else the first file's.

categoryId.description: A things category (slates_list_library) to file the product in. Defaults to Products.

itemId.description: A thing already in the Library (slates_list_library) to fill from the page instead of making a product.

brand.description: false: make no look for the brand. Default true.

maxPictures.description: How many pictures to fetch from the page. Default 6; the desktop takes at most 12.

tools.name: slates_update_storyboard
tools.description: Update a board's name and/or description.

tools.name: slates_delete_storyboard
tools.description: Delete a board with all its scenes and Shots; the media they made stays, and a Shot that also sits on another board survives. The app cannot undo this, so confirm with the user first.

tools.name: slates_update_scene
tools.description: Update a scene's name and/or position within its board.

tools.name: slates_delete_scene
tools.description: Delete a scene and every Shot in it; the pictures and clips they made stay in Media. The app cannot undo this, so confirm with the user first. To drop only the scene break and keep its Shots, use slates_merge_scene.

tools.name: slates_reorder_scenes
tools.description: Reorder the scenes of a board. Pass the COMPLETE list of the board's scene ids in the desired order.

tools.name: slates_update_frame
tools.description: Update a slot: its shot label, notes, bound asset (assetId=null unbinds), scene or position. A scene or position change carries the words in this slot with it on the Script page. preferredClipId picks the clip the timeline takes for this slot (a video asset id or VID code; null goes back to the newest linked video), as the take menu's "Use in the timeline" does. The BEAT — its line, references, model, prompt and framing — lives on the Shot in this slot; use slates_update_shot for that.

assetId.description: Asset UUID, not a badge code: pass the code to slates_list_assets as search to resolve it.

preferredClipId.description: The clip the timeline takes for this slot: a video asset id or badge code in the project; null clears it.

tools.name: slates_batch_update_frames
tools.description: Update MANY slots in one call — shot labels, notes, asset binding, scene/position, and preferredClipId (the clip the timeline takes for the slot: a video asset id or VID code, null to clear). Prefer this over repeated slates_update_frame when re-arranging a scene: it is one round-trip and one UI refresh, and every id is validated before anything is written, so the batch never lands half-applied. A scene or position change carries the words in each slot with it on the Script page. To write the BEATS themselves, use slates_create_shot / slates_update_shot.

assetId.description: Asset UUID, not a badge code: pass the code to slates_list_assets as search to resolve it.

preferredClipId.description: A video asset id or badge code in the project; null clears it.

tools.name: slates_delete_frame
tools.description: Delete a Shot by deleting its slot (frame): this is the delete-Shot tool, and it also removes an exploration slot. The takes stay in Media. The user can press Ctrl+Z in the app to bring a deleted Shot back.

tools.name: slates_create_shot
tools.description: Write one beat of the piece — a Shot: its script line, its references with their roles, its model and params, and the prompt that fires. It needs NO image to exist, so a whole film can be written, arranged and priced before anything is generated. It lands in the board automatically (the open scene, else the most recent board) — never unfiled. Saves only: it generates and spends nothing; price with slates_get_board_quote and fire with slates_generate_from_shots after the user approves. shotSize and camera are FREE TEXT and are never rejected or rewritten. They are bucketed only for the variety count — shot size into wide / medium / close / extreme-close / other, camera into static / push / pull / handheld / orbit / crane / other — and anything unrecognised counts as "other", which is a fine answer.

name.description: What to call it. Shown on the card; the prompt supplies one if you omit it.

prompt.description: The RAW prompt, @mentions intact. Never write "image 1" yourself — the composer numbers references, and a hand-written number is wrong the moment one moves. Required unless fromAssetId supplies the recipe.

fromAssetId.description: Save as shot: start from this asset's RECORDED recipe (UUID or badge code) — its prompt, model, settings and references — as Media's Save as shot does. That result becomes the Shot's first take unless another Shot already holds it. Anything else you pass overrides the recipe.

model.description: Model id — the same ids slates_generate_image / slates_generate_video / slates_generate_audio take, and their descriptions carry the routing. Optional: a Shot can be planned before the model is decided.

aspectRatio.description: Validated against the model; see slates_generate_video.

duration.description: Seconds for video or duration-based audio; TTS uses text length.

videoResolution.description: Validated against the model when the Shot is saved.

detachedVoiceCharacterIds.description: Character voices removed from this recipe.

seedanceFace.description: Seedance only — a reference shows an AI character's face; without it faces are blocked. The estimate prices it.

audioDurationSeconds.description: Audio lane. On seed-audio the requested duration IS the bill.

gridMode.description: Image models: a grid of takes in one picture.

audioPromptInfluence.description: eleven-sfx: how literally the prompt is followed.

reference.description: Plain reference images, in send order — cited in the prompt as "image 1", "image 2"… UUIDs or badge codes ("IMG-A8").

subject.description: Reference images that ARE the subject — composed as "Image N is the subject", so the model knows who the shot is about. UUIDs or badge codes ("IMG-A8").

style.description: Reference images the look is taken from — composed as one trailing "Render in the visual style of image N" clause. UUIDs or badge codes ("IMG-A8").

video-reference.description: Reference CLIPS read alongside the images — cited as "video 1", "video 2"… UUIDs or badge codes ("IMG-A8").

audio-reference.description: Reference AUDIO clips — cited as "audio 1", "audio 2"…. Pair each with audioRefSpokenText when it contains speech. UUIDs or badge codes ("IMG-A8").

refs.description: Attachments by ROLE, ordered within each role. The role decides the sentence the model is told, so a subject reference and a plain one are not interchangeable.

firstFrameAssetId.description: Starting frame for image-to-video (UUID or badge code).

audioRefSpokenText.description: Same order and length as refs["audio-reference"]; use "" for a clip with no words. The model RE-TRANSCRIBES a supplied take, so only text decides the words.

characterIds.description: Characters the prompt @mentions — stored as ENTITY ids, so updating the character updates every Shot that names it.

frameId.description: Put it in this exact frame. Optional — omit it and the Shot files itself into a scene, creating a board if there is none.

sceneId.description: File it into this scene. Optional; ignored when frameId is given.

storyboardId.description: File it into this board (its last scene, or a new one). Optional; ignored when frameId or sceneId is given.

position.description: Slot in the scene it files into, 0 = first. Omit to file it last.

speaker.description: Speaker: character id, bare name (including a new character), or "VO". Null when silent.

line.description: Words spoken verbatim; no camera or scene instructions.

delivery.description: Optional performance note. Leave null unless a specific direction is needed; do not fill every line with stock adjectives. Not sent to TTS: put supported inline cues in the spoken text using the selected model's prompting guide.

action.description: Screenplay action covering everyone in frame.

prop.description: The readable object carrying the beat.

shotSize.description: Free-text framing, e.g. "wide" or "long-lens CU, other head blurred"; bucketed only for variety counts.

camera.description: Free-text camera move, e.g. "slow push in"; never rejected or rewritten.

recipeMode.description: Script mode compiles active words with production fields. Custom keeps the authored prompt exactly.

promptScriptLine.description: The exact script line reviewed when authoring this custom prompt.

continues.description: True when this line continues the previous row: one sentence across two cuts.

tools.name: slates_update_shot
tools.description: Change part of a Shot, or attach/detach it from a board frame — anything you omit is left exactly as it was. Saves only: it generates and spends nothing. shotSize and camera are FREE TEXT and are never rejected or rewritten. They are bucketed only for the variety count — shot size into wide / medium / close / extreme-close / other, camera into static / push / pull / handheld / orbit / crane / other — and anything unrecognised counts as "other", which is a fine answer.

shotId.description: The Shot id, or its SHOT-A code as shown on the row.

projectId.description: The Shot's project — badge codes and entity ids resolve against it.

detachedVoiceCharacterIds.description: Character voices removed from this recipe.

params.description: Same shape as slates_create_shot — see it for what each field means. Generation settings for the Shot.

refs.description: Same shape as slates_create_shot — see it for what each field means. Attachments by ROLE, ordered within each role. The role decides the sentence the model is told, so a subject reference and a plain one are not interchangeable.

attachFrameId.description: Attach this Shot to a board frame.

detachFrameId.description: Detach it from a frame. Not its last one: pass attachFrameId too, or delete the Shot.

posterAssetId.description: Which reference represents this Shot as a thumbnail. Defaulted automatically (first frame, else the first image reference, else the newest take) — only set it to OVERRIDE, and pass null to go back to the default.

recipeMode.description: Script mode compiles active words with production fields. Custom keeps the authored prompt exactly.

promptScriptLine.description: The exact script line reviewed when authoring this custom prompt.

tools.name: slates_duplicate_shot
tools.description: Fork a saved Shot, changing the prompt, the model or any param on the COPY in the same call — make one, fork it five times, change one thing on each. The original is never touched.

shotId.description: The Shot id, or its SHOT-A code.

name.description: Name for the copy (default: the original plus "copy").

prompt.description: Replace the prompt on the copy. Omit to keep the original's.

model.description: Point the copy at a different model — the A/B lever. The prompt is NOT rewritten, and the copy records which model it was written for.

detachedVoiceCharacterIds.description: Character voices removed from this recipe.

params.description: Same shape as slates_create_shot — see it for what each field means. Generation settings for the Shot.

frameId.description: Attach the copy to this frame. Omit to keep the original's frame; pass null to leave it unattached.

tools.name: slates_split_shot
tools.description: Split one Shot into two at a caret in its line. The text after the caret moves to the new Shot, which INHERITS the model, params and references and lands directly after it in the scene. A mid-sentence split marks the second row as continuing the first — one sentence, two cuts, which is the signature voiceover move. Takes stay with the first row. Omit the caret to add a sibling cut with the same visuals and no words moved.

shotId.description: The Shot id, or its SHOT-A code.

caret.description: Character offset into the Shot's `line` to cut at. Omitted = the end of the line.

tools.name: slates_merge_shots
tools.description: Merge two adjacent Shots into one. Texts join, references union, the FIRST Shot's model and params win, and the durations SUM — which may exceed the model's window, in which case it is shown and never blocked. Lossy in one direction: the second Shot's model and params are discarded. There is no undo op; the user can press Ctrl+Z in the app straight after, and the takes stay as the history.

firstId.description: The Shot that survives — its model and params win. Id or SHOT-A code.

secondId.description: The Shot folded into it. Id or SHOT-A code.

tools.name: slates_split_take
tools.description: Move a take to a NEW Shot made from its recorded recipe (to move it to an existing Shot, use slates_refile_take). The result (a take under `shotId`) moves to a new Shot whose recipe is the take's RECORDED one — the prompt, model, params and references it was actually made from, which may differ from what the source Shot says now. The new Shot lands directly after the source by default; the source keeps its other takes and its recipe untouched, and is never deleted when emptied. Script fields (line, speaker) start empty on the new row.

shotId.description: The source Shot id, or its SHOT-A code.

assetId.description: The take to move — an asset id or its IMG-A / VID-A code. Must be a take of `shotId`.

sceneId.description: Scene for the new Shot. Omitted = the source's scene.

position.description: Frame position in that scene. Omitted = directly after the source.

name.description: The new Shot's name. Omitted = the take's label or the first 60 characters of its prompt.

tools.name: slates_refile_take
tools.description: Move a take (a result) from one Shot to another in the same project. Only the attribution moves: neither Shot's recipe changes, the asset stays where it is in Media, and a clip that a frame prefers keeps that role. `fromShotId` is a guard — the take moves only if it still hangs under that Shot (omit it to claim an unattributed result). An emptied Shot is kept, never deleted. To start a new Shot from the take, use slates_split_take.

assetId.description: The take — an asset id or its IMG-A / VID-A code.

fromShotId.description: The Shot it hangs under now (id or SHOT-A code). Omitted or null = an unattributed result.

toShotId.description: The Shot to move it to (id or SHOT-A code).

tools.name: slates_get_script
tools.description: A scene's script, the one text its Shots' lines are ranges of, with every ranged Shot's [start, end) offsets and code. For the whole board's document (headings, formatting, every scene) use slates_get_script_document. Read this before slates_edit_script or slates_make_shot_from_script: offsets are character positions into exactly this text. Text no Shot holds is unshot; a Shot listed by slates_list_shots but absent here has no words on the page yet. `rev` names this exact text and `revision` the whole script document: pass either to slates_edit_script so an edit measured on it is refused, not misplaced, if the words changed in between.

sceneId.description: The scene (slates_get_storyboard_with_frames lists them, each with its script).

tools.name: slates_get_script_uses
tools.description: Review each reused passage before updating it: current and proposed words, destination revision, and local-edit conflicts. Pass only explicitly selected non-conflicting uses to slates_update_script_section (updateUses). sectionId comes from slates_get_script_sections.

tools.name: slates_get_shot_inputs
tools.description: Read this Shot's take input history and the finished takes elsewhere in the project made from its exact inputs; add one free with slates_reuse_shot_take. Earlier and unknown inputs remain playable but never count as a match. No generation.

tools.name: slates_reuse_shot_take
tools.description: Explicitly link a take with matching saved request and recipe inputs to this shot. Keeps the original generation and independent shot recipe. Input changes are rechecked before reuse; costs no credits. Find candidates with slates_get_shot_inputs; slates_refile_take moves a take instead.

assetId.description: Asset UUID or badge code from compatibleTakes.

tools.name: slates_preview_script_variation
tools.description: Preview explicit version choices (one saved version per section) and independent ID-based reference replacements without writes or generation. An optional ordered arrangement supports repetition and omission. Returns composed requests, custom-prompt/reference warnings, a quote, and a plan marking each shot reuse (a finished take with matching inputs exists) or new. Inspect only the combinations you need.

expectedRevision.description: The revision from slates_get_script_document; a stale one is refused.

choices.description: One saved version per section, ids from slates_get_script_sections.

itemOverrides.description: Swap one Library item for another of the same kind and role, a person for a person, a location for a location (item ids). voice keep: the replaced item's voice stays on the Shots it speaks in; replace: it does not carry over.

assetOverrides.description: Swap one asset for another of the same type (ids or badge codes).

idempotencyKey.description: Required to create: a retry with the same key and choices returns the same Board.

tools.name: slates_create_script_variation
tools.description: Materialize one reviewed variation as an independent Board with local shot IDs and lineage. Pass idempotencyKey: a retry with the same key returns the same Board. Returns a quote through the normal request service. No media generation or implicit take reuse.

expectedRevision.description: The revision from slates_get_script_document; a stale one is refused.

choices.description: One saved version per section, ids from slates_get_script_sections.

itemOverrides.description: Swap one Library item for another of the same kind and role, a person for a person, a location for a location (item ids). voice keep: the replaced item's voice stays on the Shots it speaks in; replace: it does not carry over.

assetOverrides.description: Swap one asset for another of the same type (ids or badge codes).

idempotencyKey.description: Required to create: a retry with the same key and choices returns the same Board.

tools.name: slates_get_script_sections
tools.description: Read free-named script sections, anchored fragments, saved versions and local-change state.

tools.name: slates_update_script_section
tools.description: Create a free-named section from a selected passage, save the words now on the page as a new version (action alternative), save changes to the shown version (save) or choose another (choose), insert an editable copy (reuse), update unedited copies (updateUses), rename or archive a section or one version (alternativeId), or set its free tags (action tags). Choosing, archiving a section, reuse and updateUses first save the page's words and shot bindings into the version that was showing (the page is never unsaved; save remains for an explicit save), and only alternative starts a new version; archiving a section keeps its words, shots and media on the page. Uses the current document revision and never generates media. Partial crossing sections are refused.

expectedRevision.description: The revision from slates_get_script_document; a stale one is refused.

parentId.description: create: a section that contains this passage.

label.description: The name: required for create and alternative, and for rename.

tags.description: Free tags for action tags; replaces the list.

target.description: reuse: the scene the copy goes into, the place in its text, and that board's document revision.

uses.description: updateUses: the copies to update, with the revisions slates_get_script_uses returns.

fragments.description: create: the passage, as ranges of scene text.

tools.name: slates_get_script_suggestions
tools.description: Read suggested replacements on a script: pending ones first (stale when their words changed since), then recent accepted or dismissed ones.

tools.name: slates_update_script_suggestions
tools.description: Propose replacements for exact passages without editing the script (create), or accept or dismiss one. Use create when asked to suggest or improve a passage; the creator reviews and accepts it in the document. Each quotes the words it replaces; one whose words change later is stale and will not apply. Accepting is one undoable write. Never generates media.

original.description: The exact words now at start to end.

tools.name: slates_get_script_document
tools.description: Read the whole script document: scene strings, UTF-16 block/shot anchors, non-spoken headings/directions and a revision for safe writes. Formatting metadata contains no second copy of paragraph text. slates_get_script reads one scene's text with its Shot offsets.

tools.name: slates_update_script_document
tools.description: Several script changes in one revision-checked write: ordered text edits across scenes, formatting, moving a block, making Shots from ranges (makeShots), splitting or merging scenes (sceneAction). For one text replacement in one scene use slates_edit_script. Read the document first. Stale writes are refused without replacing either author’s work. A move carries contained shot anchors; restoreRevision restores an existing text/structure revision. No generation side effect. ensureScene creates an empty scene only if needed.

tools.name: slates_edit_script
tools.description: One text replacement in one scene (for several edits, formatting or scene changes in one write, use slates_update_script_document): one contiguous replacement — `removed` characters at `at` become `text` (insert: removed 0; delete: text ''). Every Shot's range follows the way comment anchors follow a document: text before a Shot moves it, text after leaves it, an edit inside grows or shrinks it, typing at its end extends it unless the text starts a new line, and deleting all of a Shot's words leaves it with no words and no place on the page. Every affected Shot's `line` changes at once: this is editing the Shots. Read slates_get_script first; offsets are into that text. Pass its `rev` (or the document `revision` as `expectedRevision`): when the Script page or anything else changed the words since, the edit is refused ('the script changed since you read it', or SCRIPT_CONFLICT for a stale revision), and you re-read and measure again. The result carries the new `rev` and `revision` for a following edit.

expectedRevision.description: The document `revision` slates_get_script or slates_get_script_document returned. The edit is refused if the document changed since.

at.description: Character offset the replacement starts at.

removed.description: How many characters to remove there (0 to insert).

text.description: What goes in their place ('' to delete). A blank line (\n\n) separates paragraphs.

rev.description: The `rev` slates_get_script (or the previous edit) returned. The edit is refused if the text changed since.

tools.name: slates_make_shot_from_script
tools.description: Turn a selected passage of a scene's script into Shots, as the Script page's popover does; start and end are offsets into slates_get_script's text. The action follows what the selection touches: Make shot when the selection touches no Shot; Split when it lies inside one Shot (the Shot keeps its first piece and its takes, every other piece becomes a new Shot after it); Extend when it crosses one Shot's edge; Merge when it spans several (the first takes the span — unshot text between them included, nothing deleted — the others give up their words: one holding a take (finished or generating), a prompt, a reference or a picture stays and waits for text; only a completely blank one is removed). Pass `waitingShotId` to give a Shot that has no words yet (made on the Board, split off a take) the selected text instead. `perParagraph: true` over several unshot paragraphs makes one Shot per paragraph. A new Shot is filed after every ranged Shot whose words start before it.

waitingShotId.description: A Shot with no words (id or SHOT-A code) that should take the selection.

perParagraph.description: Over unshot text spanning several paragraphs: one Shot per paragraph.

tools.name: slates_break_script_into_shots
tools.description: "Break the script into shots": a Shot for every piece of text no Shot holds — one per paragraph — across a whole board, or one scene. Shots that already exist keep their words. This is the cut after the script is right; slates_paste_script is the step before it.

tools.name: slates_split_scene
tools.description: Open a scene at a heading line: the text from `lineEnd` on moves into a NEW scene directly after this one, with its Shots and their slots; the heading line [lineStart, lineEnd) itself is consumed and `name` becomes the new scene's name. Use slates_paste_script to do this for every SCENE / INT. / EXT. / # line of a pasted script at once.

lineStart.description: Offset where the heading line starts.

lineEnd.description: Offset just past the heading line (the newline after it is consumed too).

name.description: The new scene's name. Omitted = 'Scene N'.

tools.name: slates_merge_scene
tools.description: Join a scene to the one before it (Backspace in an emptied heading): the texts join with a blank line, every Shot keeps its words and its slot appends after the previous scene's. Only the scene row goes — no Shot does. Returns the offset in the joined script where this scene's text now starts.

tools.name: slates_paste_script
tools.description: Dump a script in as TEXT, not Shots: the text lands in the scene's script (at its end by default), and lines reading `SCENE …`, `INT.` / `EXT.` / `I/E.` or `# Name` open scenes. No Shot is made — cutting is the writer's act or yours: slates_break_script_into_shots for one per paragraph, or slates_make_shot_from_script per selection. With no sceneId, a new scene at the end of the board takes the text (dropped again if the script opens with its own heading). Prefer this over slates_create_shot per paragraph: see the whole script, get it right, then cut it.

storyboardId.description: The board, when no scene is named.

sceneId.description: The scene to paste into. Omitted = a new scene at the end.

text.description: The script. Blank lines separate paragraphs.

at.description: Offset in the scene's script to paste at. Omitted = the end.

tools.name: slates_list_shots
tools.description: Read the shot list — every Shot as a compact row in board order (scene, then position), with its place on the board (2C: scene number and slot letter, as the window shows it and the user says it), the piece's cut count, runtime, saved-recipe price and its variety distribution. Read this before firing a set: if one shot size is the plurality or three cuts in a row share a camera move, the batch is wrong before a credit is spent.

frameId.description: Only Shots attached to this frame.

tools.name: slates_get_shot
tools.description: Read one Shot in full — the COMPOSED prompt the request will actually carry, its numbered references, anything it points at that no longer exists, its exact credit quote, and its place on the board (2C, as the window shows it). Audit your own work here before firing.

shotId.description: The Shot id, or its SHOT-A code as shown on the row.

tools.name: slates_use_pictures_as_first_frames
tools.description: The Board's 'Use pictures as first frames': each video Shot that has a picture and no first frame starts its video from that picture (its tile picture, else its newest picture take; a picture that was its only plain Reference moves into the frame slot). Nothing is generated and nothing is charged. Pass shotIds (ids or SHOT-A codes) to act on those Shots; omit them to act on every Shot of the board open in the window, as the command does (open one with slates_set_view first). shotIds.description: Only these Shots. Omit for every Shot of the board open in the window.

tools.name: slates_generate_from_shots
tools.description: Generate results for saved Shots, spending credits. Call without confirm for the itemized prices the Generate panel shows and a fingerprint; show the user the total and wait for their OK, then pass confirm with that fingerprint. Changed recipes require a fresh price. Runs sequentially; after a timeout inspect generations (slates_list_generations, status processing) instead of re-firing. Pass draft to generate previews instead: one picture for each Shot that has none, kept as a take of that Shot; the Shot's recipe does not change.
